source.title: Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes
readSections: Read in full in arXiv:1810.04493v2 (3 September 2020), whose abstract page describes it as "24 pages; final version, to appear in Duke Mathematical Journal": §1 Macaulayfication as a weak form of resolution of singularities; §2 (S₂)-ification of coherent modules; §3 Ubiquity of Cohen–Macaulay blowing ups; §4 Macaulayfication in the local case; §5 Macaulayfication in the global case; and the bibliography.

Sources read: the arXiv e-print archive of v2, sha256 8704c071cf1029ba386764f13841d3871ea79d49c2b2af920086da4789dbd088, whose two files are macaulayfication.tex (2045 lines) and bibliography.ltb; the compiled arXiv PDF of v2, sha256 a07d62e6ef1e4c2126c172426391e97031d28006b92ccb6c5f3afd9c2ddb07b9, 24 pages; and the author's copy of the published version, https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~kestutis.cesnavicius/macaulayfication.pdf, sha256 55ded201a17ae161400c1989d67ad7a09356c23f87b2e88eef2e763632939ac6, read 2026-09-23, whose listing on the author's publications page records Duke Mathematical Journal 170 (2021), no. 7, 1419–1455.

Version check: the two PDFs were compared word by word after extracting the text from the content streams of both. Apart from line breaking and hyphenation they agree; no statement, hypothesis or reference differs, and both carry the two misprints recorded below. The numbering of the 53 numbered items of the paper was re-derived from the LaTeX — the class puts theorems, propositions, lemmas, corollaries, definitions, examples, remarks and the unnamed numbered paragraphs on the subsection counter, with the numbered items of the \brems and \begs lists stepping it through \addtocounter, and equations numbered within it — and every one of the 42 numbered statements was located at its predicted number in the arXiv PDF; the four not found by that search are exactly the four remarks that are list items inside \brems blocks and are therefore printed as bare numbers.

Mechanical audits of the LaTeX source, all clean: no duplicate \lab, no undefined \ref or \Cref, and no cross-reference whose introducing word disagrees with the environment carrying the target label (the six apparent mismatches are all \remi list items correctly referred to as Remarks).

summary:
Česnavičius proves that Macaulayfication exists in complete generality. A Macaulayfication of a scheme X is a proper birational map X̃ → X with X̃ Cohen–Macaulay that is an isomorphism over the Cohen–Macaulay locus CM(X); it is the Cohen–Macaulay analogue of Grothendieck's resolution conjecture, proposed by Faltings, and reduces resolution of singularities to the Cohen–Macaulay case. The main theorem (Theorem 1.6, in the precise form Theorem 5.3) produces one for every CM-quasi-excellent Noetherian scheme, with the map projective and with finitely many prescribed coherent modules carried along. CM-quasi-excellence — Cohen–Macaulay formal fibres, and a nonempty Cohen–Macaulay open in every integral closed subscheme — is weaker than quasi-excellence, so the theorem is new even for Q-schemes, and Proposition 5.5 shows it is exactly the right hypothesis. The corollaries are proper flat Cohen–Macaulay integral models over a Dedekind base (Corollary 1.8), Cohen–Macaulay principalisation (Corollary 1.10) and Cohen–Macaulay compactifications (Corollary 1.11).

The proof has three parts. §2 constructs a noncanonical (S_2)-ification: an (S_1)-ification always exists, and for an (S_2)-quasi-excellent scheme a finite birational (S_2) modification exists (Theorem 2.13, Corollary 2.14), built by Noetherian induction, formal patching and Kollár's coherence criterion for j_*; this reduces the problem to CM-excellent, locally equidimensional schemes, using Ratliff's theorem and the fact that an (S_2) scheme with (S_2) formal fibres is formally equidimensional. §3 reviews Kawasaki's theory: secant and CM-secant sequences, the annihilator identity for local cohomology against a normalized dualizing complex, d-sequences and the Goto–Yamagishi equalities, and Kawasaki's theorem that for a CM-secant sequence the strict transform Bl_I(M) along I = ∏_i (r_1,…,r_i) is Cohen–Macaulay. §§4–5 run the induction: over a complete local base, with the special fibre already a divisor and its complement Cohen–Macaulay, one builds a decreasing chain of biequidimensional subschemes using the Gabber–Liu–Lorenzini avoidance lemma, so that the local generators form a CM-secant sequence at every point and Kawasaki's theorem applies to the product ideal (Proposition 4.4); Noetherian induction and the composition of blowing ups then globalise it (Proposition 5.2).

The paper needs: excellence and its CM- and (S_n)- variants with formal fibres; catenarity, local and formal equidimensionality and Ratliff's theorem; the openness of the (S_n) and Cohen–Macaulay loci; local cohomology with its Čech and spectral-sequence calculus; dualizing complexes over Noetherian rings and schemes, with Kawasaki's theorem settling Sharp's conjecture; blowing up, strict transforms in the sense of Raynaud–Gruson, and the composition of two blowing ups; the Nagata compactification; Kollár's coherence criterion for pushforward along an open immersion; the Gabber–Liu–Lorenzini avoidance lemma; and Kawasaki's construction of Cohen–Macaulay blowing ups, which is the only source of Cohen–Macaulayness in the argument.

After review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): 81 items (3 library, 5 planned, 73 missing), 6 routes, all accepted as corrected. The three recorded mistakes are confirmed; E4–E9 are new: misprints in the Cohen–Macaulay condition of §1.14, Remark 3.9, Proposition 3.11(iii), the ideal I_s and (3.14.10) of the proof of Theorem 3.14, and an error in (4.4.1) of the proof of Proposition 4.4 (the product of annihilators must be taken in O_X, not as a preimage), repaired in one line. No stated result changes. Local cohomology beyond Mathlib, secant sequences and the injective hull go to R03.3 (route 4) and dualizing complexes to AS.1 (route 5), where accepted routes already put them; the Nagata compactification is planned in L2 and blowups in Tau Ceti StableReduction Layer 4; the commutative Part II is narrowed to Kawasaki's Cohen–Macaulay blowing ups.

items.name: Quasi-excellent and excellent schemes
items.statement: A scheme X is quasi-excellent if it is locally Noetherian, for each x ∈ X the geometric fibres of Spec(Ô_{X,x}) → Spec(O_{X,x}) — the formal fibres of X at x — are regular, and every integral X-scheme X' finite over some affine open of X has a nonempty regular open subscheme. For such an X the regular locus Reg(X) is open. A quasi-excellent X is excellent if it is in addition universally catenary.
items.locator: §1, the footnote to Conjecture 1.1, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (EGA IV₂ 7.8.2, 7.8.5; Illusie–Laszlo–Orgogozo I.2.10, I.7.1)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): ring-level excellence and catenarity belong to Commutative algebra for deformation theory and patching R03.3, whose text says to 'state hypotheses on catenarity and excellence rather than importing geometric conclusions'; RS-08 keeps that clause, AUDIT-17 records 'Catenarity and excellence as explicit hypotheses' as absent, and PAPER-BOCKLE-IYENGAR-PASKUNAS-23/088 and PAPER-PASKUNAS-QUAST-26/76 are already sourced into R03.3 as missing. Route 1 imports the ring-level notions and builds only the scheme-level definitions and the openness of Reg(X) here: Tau Ceti ModularCurves 4D plans that openness only for schemes locally of finite type over an excellent base. Mathlib has regular local rings and regular rings (IsRegularLocalRing, IsRegularRing, RingTheory/RegularLocalRing/Defs.lean:51, 92).

items.name: Conjecture 1.1: resolution of singularities in Grothendieck's formulation
items.statement: Conjecture 1.1. For a quasi-excellent, reduced, Noetherian scheme X there are a regular scheme X̃ and a proper morphism π : X̃ → X that is an isomorphism over the regular locus Reg(X). It is known for Q-schemes by Temkin's theorem building on Hironaka; in positive and mixed characteristic it is open apart from low-dimensional cases and variants such as alterations. By Proposition 2.7 one may reduce it to the case when X is excellent and locally equidimensional.
items.locator: Conjecture 1.1 with the two paragraphs following it, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (EGA IV₂ 7.9.6; Temkin, Theorem 1.1; Hironaka; de Jong)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): an open conjecture, recorded so that the design job states it and Proposition 2.7's reduction; nothing plans a proof, and none should be planned. Algebraic moduli R09.7 plans resolution only for varieties of finite type over a field of characteristic zero, and Temkin's theorem for quasi-excellent Q-schemes is unplanned.

items.name: CM-quasi-excellent and CM-excellent schemes
items.statement: Definition 1.2. A scheme X is CM-quasi-excellent if it is locally Noetherian and (1) the formal fibres of the local rings of X are Cohen–Macaulay and (2) every integral, closed subscheme X' ⊂ X has a nonempty, Cohen–Macaulay open subscheme; it is CM-excellent if in addition it is universally catenary. Condition (2) alone already implies that the Cohen–Macaulay locus CM(X) is open.
items.locator: Definition 1.2 with the sentence following it, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455

items.name: Example 1.3: quasi-excellent and Dedekind schemes are CM-quasi-excellent
items.statement: Example 1.3. Every quasi-excellent scheme is CM-quasi-excellent, and likewise for excellence. In contrast to the existence of non-excellent discrete valuation rings, caused by the possible inseparability of the field extension obtained by completing the fraction field, every Dedekind scheme — a Noetherian normal scheme of dimension ≤ 1 — is CM-excellent.
items.locator: Example 1.3, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455

items.name: Remark 1.4: quasi-Cohen–Macaulay schemes and their closed subschemes
items.statement: Remark 1.4. Every Cohen–Macaulay scheme is CM-excellent. More generally, if a locally Noetherian X is quasi-Cohen–Macaulay, that is, carries a coherent Cohen–Macaulay O_X-module 𝓜 with Supp(𝓜) = X, then every closed subscheme of X is CM-excellent: EGA IV₂ 6.3.8 and 6.11.9(ii) give conditions (1) and (2) of Definition 1.2 and the universal catenarity follows from the proof of EGA IV₂ 6.3.7, which continues to work in the quasi-Cohen–Macaulay case.
items.locator: Remark 1.4, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455

items.name: Remark 1.5: stability of CM-quasi-excellence
items.statement: Remark 1.5. If X is CM-quasi-excellent then so is every localisation of a locally finite type X-scheme, by EGA IV₂ 7.4.4 (with 7.3.8) for the formal-fibre condition and 6.11.9(i) for the open-CM-subscheme condition.
items.locator: Remark 1.5, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455

items.name: Theorem 1.6: existence of a Macaulayfication
items.statement: Theorem 1.6. For every CM-quasi-excellent, Noetherian scheme X there are a Cohen–Macaulay scheme X̃ and a birational, projective morphism π : X̃ → X that is an isomorphism over the Cohen–Macaulay locus CM(X) ⊂ X.
items.locator: Theorem 1.6, proved as Theorem 5.3 with Remark 5.4, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455

items.name: Remark 1.7: arranging the preimage of the non-CM locus to be a divisor
items.statement: Remark 1.7. For any fixed closed subscheme Z ⊂ X whose support is X \ CM(X), one may arrange in addition that the scheme-theoretic preimage of Z in X̃ is a divisor with support X̃ \ CM(X): since π is birational and X̃ has no embedded associated primes, the preimage of any divisor in X is a divisor in X̃, so it suffices to apply Theorem 1.6 with Bl_Z(X) in place of X.
items.locator: Remark 1.7, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455

items.name: Corollary 1.8: proper flat Cohen–Macaulay integral models
items.statement: Corollary 1.8. For every integral Dedekind scheme S with function field K and every proper, Cohen–Macaulay K-scheme X there is a proper, flat, Cohen–Macaulay S-scheme 𝒳 with 𝒳_K ≅ X; if X is projective over K then 𝒳 may be chosen projective over S. (S is CM-excellent by Example 1.3; one applies Theorem 1.6 to the schematic image 𝒳_0 of X in a Nagata compactification over S, after spreading X out, and uses that 𝒳_0 is S-flat with K-fibre X; for the projective statement one forms the schematic image in a projective space instead.)
items.locator: Corollary 1.8 with the paragraph after it, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455

items.name: Remark 1.9: extending Cohen–Macaulay modules to the integral model
items.statement: Remark 1.9. If X in Corollary 1.8 comes equipped with a finite family of coherent Cohen–Macaulay modules, for instance vector bundles, then the finer form of Theorem 1.6 given in Theorem 5.3 lets one arrange in addition that they extend to Cohen–Macaulay modules on 𝒳.
items.locator: Remark 1.9, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455

items.name: Corollary 1.10: Cohen–Macaulay principalisation
items.statement: Corollary 1.10. For every Noetherian, Cohen–Macaulay scheme X and every closed subscheme Z ⊂ X there are a Cohen–Macaulay scheme X̃ and a projective morphism X̃ → X such that the scheme-theoretic preimage of Z in X̃ is a divisor and X̃ → X is an isomorphism over the maximal open U ⊂ X on which Z is already a divisor. (Both X and Bl_Z(X) are CM-excellent and locally equidimensional by Remark 1.4 and Lemma 2.3(b); one applies Theorem 5.3 to Bl_Z(X).)
items.locator: Corollary 1.10 with the paragraph after it, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455

items.name: Corollary 1.11: Cohen–Macaulay compactifications
items.statement: Corollary 1.11. For every CM-quasi-excellent Noetherian scheme S and every finite type, separated, Cohen–Macaulay S-scheme X there is an open S-immersion X ↪ X̄ into a proper, Cohen–Macaulay S-scheme X̄ such that X̄ \ X is (the support of) a possibly nonreduced divisor in X̄ [the paper prints 'in X'; sourceIssues E1]. It follows by combining the Nagata compactification with Theorem 1.6 and Corollary 1.10.
items.locator: Corollary 1.11, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): the statement now carries the correction of E1, which it had dropped along with the ambient scheme.

items.name: The Nagata compactification theorem
items.statement: Every separated, finite type morphism of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes factors as an open immersion followed by a proper morphism. The paper uses it three times: to form the schematic image 𝒳_0 in Corollary 1.8, to produce the compactification of Corollary 1.11, and to deduce in §4.2 that every finite type separated scheme over a Noetherian scheme with a dualizing complex again has one.
items.locator: Used in Corollaries 1.8 and 1.11 and in §4.2, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (Deligne, Le théorème de plongement de Nagata, Kyoto J. Math. 50 (2010), 1.6)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): the status was missing; it is planned. Adic coefficients and comparison with schemes L2 plans the compactification of separated finite-type morphisms of qcqs schemes ('This gives the nonnoetherian Nagata statement, not merely its finite-presentation special case'), consuming the Noetherian case from UPSTREAM:ECD:SCH_SUPPORT_NOETH; AUDIT-18 lists the nonnoetherian case as absent, and the accepted PAPER-BOXER-PILLONI-26/nagata-compactification is planned there. All three uses here have Noetherian bases. The item left route 3.

items.name: §1.14: support, the conditions (S_n) and Cohen–Macaulayness
items.statement: §1.14. For a coherent module 𝓜 on a locally Noetherian X, its support Supp(𝓜) ⊂ X is the closed subscheme cut out by the coherent ideal Ann_{O_X}(𝓜). For n ∈ Z, 𝓜 is (S_n) if depth_{O_x}(𝓜_x) ≥ min(n, dim(Supp(𝓜_x))) for all x ∈ X, with dim(∅) = −∞; 𝓜 is (S_1) exactly when it has no embedded associated primes (EGA IV₂ 5.7.5), and 𝓜 is Cohen–Macaulay if it is (S_n) for every n, that is, if depth_{O_x}(𝓜_x) = dim(Supp(𝓜_x)) for all x ∈ Supp(𝓜) [the paper prints 'for all x ∈ X'; sourceIssues E4]. A scheme is (S_n) or Cohen–Macaulay if it is locally Noetherian and O_X has that property.
items.locator: §1.14 (Notation and conventions), first paragraph, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (EGA IV₁ 0.14.1.2; EGA IV₂ 5.7.5)
items.note: R03.3 plans depth, Cohen–Macaulay rings and modules, associated primes and support lemmas for finite modules; SF.0 the coherent modules on schemes. The Serre condition (S_n) itself, and the sheaf-level statement that (S_1) means no embedded associated primes, are the small additions this item records and are carried by the (S_n)-loci item. Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): the Cohen–Macaulay clause is quantified over Supp(𝓜) (E4). The earlier note said (S_n) is carried by the (S_n)-loci item, but that item (§2.8) only states openness; the planning is this. R03.3 plans depth, Cohen–Macaulay rings and modules, associated primes and support for finite modules, and the Serre conditions (S_k) are planned there as in the accepted PAPER-HACON-WITASZEK-23/cm-depth; Scheme and stack foundations SF.0 plans quasi-coherent modules. Only the sheaf-level form is an addition, which route 1 states as an adapter. Mathlib has Module.support (RingTheory/Support.lean:49), Module.annihilator (RingTheory/Ideal/Maps.lean:860) and associatedPrimes (RingTheory/Ideal/AssociatedPrime/Basic.lean:103), and Rees's theorem ModuleCat.exists_isRegular_tfae (RingTheory/Depth/Rees.lean:158), but no depth.

items.name: §1.14: height, coheight, codimension and torsion submodules
items.statement: §1.14. For a scheme X the height of x ∈ X is dim(O_{X,x}) and the coheight is the dimension of the closure of {x}; X^{(i)} is the set of points of height i; the codimension of a closed Y ⊂ X is the infimum of the heights of the points of X lying on Y. For a module M over a ring R and an ideal 𝔯 one writes M⟨𝔯⟩ for the 𝔯-torsion, M⟨𝔯^∞⟩ for the union of the M⟨𝔯^n⟩, and M' :_M 𝔯 for the preimage of (M/M')⟨𝔯⟩ in M; R̂ is the completion of a local ring R.
items.locator: §1.14 (Notation and conventions), second and third paragraphs, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: R09.7a plans blowups by the Rees algebra with their projective universal property, affine charts and base-change comparison; SF.0 relative Proj. What R09.7a states in the characteristic-zero resolution setting is used here for an arbitrary Noetherian scheme and an arbitrary finite-type ideal, which is the same construction. Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): the item was split: blowing up is now item 62, planned in Tau Ceti StableReduction Layers 4 and 2. The former citation of Algebraic moduli R09.7a was wrong: R09.7a plans only 'smooth base-change comparison', and R09.7 is scoped to varieties over a field of characteristic zero, while the paper uses flat base change. What remains is in Mathlib: ringKrullDim (RingTheory/KrullDimension/Basic.lean:29); ringKrullDim_stalk_eq_coheight (AlgebraicGeometry/Properties.lean:376), which says dim O_{X,x} = Order.coheight x in Mathlib's specialisation order, so the paper's height is Mathlib's coheight and conversely; Order.height and Order.coheight (Order/KrullDimension.lean:89, 102); Ideal.height (RingTheory/Ideal/Height.lean:36); Submodule.torsionBy and torsionBySet (Algebra/Module/Torsion/Basic.lean:180, 185), with M⟨𝔯^∞⟩ the union of torsionBySet(𝔯^n); AdicCompletion (RingTheory/AdicCompletion/Basic.lean:171). X^{(i)}, the codimension of a closed subscheme and M' :_M 𝔯 are one-line definitions on top of these. Mathlib's Submodule.colon (RingTheory/Ideal/Colon.lean:35) is an ideal, not the submodule M' :_M 𝔯, and must not be used for it.

items.name: Regular sequences
items.statement: For a module M over a commutative ring R, a sequence r_1,…,r_s is M-regular if each r_i is a nonzerodivisor on M/(r_1,…,r_{i−1})M and M/(r_1,…,r_s)M ≠ 0 (weakly regular without the last condition). Regular sequences are the reference point for the secant, CM-secant and d-sequence notions of §3.
items.locator: Used throughout, in particular in §3, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: Mathlib has regular and weakly regular sequences over a commutative ring with their localisation and flat base-change stability at the pinned commit; what it does not have is depth, which is why the (S_n) item is only planned. Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): Mathlib has no depth, but it has Rees's theorem ModuleCat.exists_isRegular_tfae (RingTheory/Depth/Rees.lean:158): for finite M over Noetherian R with IM ≠ M, an M-regular sequence of length n in I exists iff Ext^i_R(R/I, M) = 0 for i < n. The three cited declarations were checked (RingTheory/Regular/RegularSequence.lean:135, 146; RingTheory/Regular/Flat.lean:47).

items.name: §2.1: universal catenarity
items.statement: §2.1. A scheme X is universally catenary if it is locally Noetherian and every scheme X' locally of finite type over X is catenary, that is, any two saturated chains of specialisations of points of X' with the same endpoints have the same length (any such chain lies in every affine open of X' containing the endpoint of larger height). Every closed subscheme of a quasi-Cohen–Macaulay scheme is universally catenary; in particular every complete Noetherian local ring is.
items.locator: §2.1 (Catenarity), Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (EGA IV₂ 5.6.3(ii))
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): catenarity of Noetherian rings is an R03.3 hypothesis (RS-08, AUDIT-17), and PAPER-BOCKLE-IYENGAR-PASKUNAS-23/028 on universally catenary schemes is already sourced into R03.3; route 1 imports the ring-level notion and builds the scheme-level universal catenarity here. The clause on closed subschemes of quasi-Cohen–Macaulay schemes is item 5 (Remark 1.4, to which the paper refers back).

items.name: §2.2: locally and formally equidimensional schemes
items.statement: §2.2. A scheme X is locally equidimensional if it is locally Noetherian and every local ring O_{X,x} is equidimensional, that is, all irreducible components of Spec(O_{X,x}) have the same dimension; X is formally equidimensional (quasi-unmixed) if it is locally Noetherian and Ô_{X,x} is equidimensional for every x.
items.locator: §2.2 (Equidimensionality), Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (EGA IV₂ 7.1.1; Herrmann–Ikeda–Orbanz 18.17; Ratliff)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): Ratliff's theorem was split off as item 63. Equidimensionality of Noetherian local rings is an R03.3 target ('Give equidimensionality, associated-prime and support lemmas for finite modules'; AUDIT-17 records that equidimensionality is not defined), and route 1 imports it. The scheme forms and formal equidimensionality (EGA IV₂ 7.1.1) are added here.

items.name: Lemma 2.3(a): formal equidimensionality is stable under locally principal divisors
items.statement: Lemma 2.3(a). Let X be a formally equidimensional scheme and 𝓘 ⊂ O_X a coherent ideal. If 𝓘 is locally principal of height > 0, then Spec(O_X/𝓘) is formally equidimensional.
items.locator: Lemma 2.3(a) with its proof, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (Herrmann–Ikeda–Orbanz 18.20; alternatively EGA IV₂ 2.3.4)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): the lemma was split: part (b) is item 64. The locator now names the sources the paper gives.

items.name: Lemma 2.4: (S_n) descends from the completion when the formal fibres are (S_n)
items.statement: Lemma 2.4. For a Noetherian local ring R with (S_n) formal fibres and an R-scheme X such that both X and X_{R̂} are locally Noetherian, a coherent O_X-module 𝓜 is (S_n) if and only if 𝓜|_{X_{R̂}} is. The 'if' direction does not need the hypothesis on the formal fibres, but the 'only if' does even for n = 1: Ferrand–Raynaud exhibited a two-dimensional Noetherian local domain that is (S_1) whose completion is not.
items.locator: Lemma 2.4 with its footnote and proof, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (EGA IV₂ 6.4.1(i), 6.4.2, 6.4.3; Ferrand–Raynaud 3.3)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): the locator now names EGA IV₂ 6.4.2, of which the proof says the claim is a special case; that input is item 72.

items.name: Lemma 2.5: an (S_2) scheme with (S_2) formal fibres is formally equidimensional
items.statement: Lemma 2.5. An (S_2) scheme whose local rings have (S_2) formal fibres is formally equidimensional.
items.locator: Lemma 2.5, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455

items.name: Remark 2.6: the hypothesis on the formal fibres cannot be dropped
items.statement: Remark 2.6. The assumption on the formal fibres cannot be dropped in Lemma 2.5: Noetherian, noncatenary, normal, local domains exist, by Ogoma's appendix or by Heitmann.
items.locator: Remark 2.6, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455

items.name: Proposition 2.7: reduction of the resolution conjecture to the excellent equidimensional case
items.statement: Proposition 2.7. For a quasi-excellent, reduced scheme X, the normalisation morphism X̃ → X is finite and an isomorphism over Reg(X), and X̃ is excellent and formally equidimensional.
items.locator: Proposition 2.7, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): the finiteness of the normalisation of a reduced excellent scheme is planned in Algebraic moduli and representability for arithmetic geometry A0-extension ('prove finite normalization under excellence'; AUDIT-01 lists it as partial), with its Nagata-ring prerequisite in R03.3 (the accepted review of PAPER-ANDRE-18-B, route 5). The construction is Mathlib's AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.normalization (AlgebraicGeometry/Normalization.lean:123). Added here: the quasi-excellent case, the isomorphism over Reg(X), and that X̃ is excellent and formally equidimensional. Route 1 imports both.

items.name: §2.8: openness of the (S_n) and Cohen–Macaulay loci
items.statement: §2.8. For a locally Noetherian X and a coherent 𝓜, the locus U_{(S_1)}(𝓜) is always open, being on each affine open the complement of the union of the closed subschemes cut out by the embedded associated primes of 𝓜. For n > 1, U_{(S_n)}(𝓜) need not be open, by Ferrand–Raynaud 3.5, which answered the question of EGA IV₂ 6.11.9(ii). However EGA IV₂ 6.11.6 makes U_{(S_n)}(𝓜) open for every coherent 𝓜 as soon as every integral closed subscheme X' ⊂ X has a nonempty (S_n) open subscheme, and EGA IV₂ 6.11.8 does the same for the Cohen–Macaulay locus CM(𝓜) under the corresponding hypothesis; both hold for CM-quasi-excellent X. One writes U_{(S_n)}(X) and CM(X) for the cases 𝓜 = O_X.
items.locator: §2.8 (Openness of the (S_n)-loci), Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (EGA IV₂ 6.11.6, 6.11.7(i), 6.11.8, 6.11.9(ii); Ferrand–Raynaud 3.5)

items.name: Theorem 2.9: existence of an (S_1)-ification
items.statement: Theorem 2.9. For a coherent module 𝓜 on a locally Noetherian scheme X, the image 𝓜' := im(𝓜 → j_*(𝓜|_{U_{(S_1)}(𝓜)})) for the open immersion j : U_{(S_1)}(𝓜) ↪ X is an (S_1)-ification of 𝓜: it is a coherent O_X-module that is (S_1) and agrees with 𝓜 on U_{(S_1)}(𝓜).
items.locator: Theorem 2.9, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455

items.name: §2.10: (S_n)-quasi-excellence
items.statement: §2.10. For n ∈ Z, a scheme X is (S_n)-quasi-excellent if it is locally Noetherian, the formal fibres of its local rings are (S_n), and every integral closed subscheme X' ⊂ X has a nonempty (S_n) open subscheme; it is (S_n)-excellent if in addition universally catenary. The second condition makes U_{(S_n)}(𝓜) open for every coherent 𝓜. A CM-quasi-excellent scheme is (S_n)-quasi-excellent for every n, and (S_n)-quasi-excellence is stable under localisation and ascends along morphisms locally of finite type.
items.locator: §2.10 ((S_n)-quasi-excellence), Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455

items.name: Lemma 2.11: extending an (S_1) or (S_2) module across an open immersion
items.statement: Lemma 2.11. For an open immersion j : U ↪ X of Noetherian, (S_2)-excellent schemes, any coherent O_U-module 𝓜 that is (S_1) (resp. (S_2)) extends to a coherent O_X-submodule 𝓜' ⊂ j_*(𝓜) that is (S_1) (resp. a finite direct sum of (S_2) modules); if 𝓜 underlies a commutative O_U-algebra then 𝓜' may be chosen to be an algebra extension, with the direct sum that of O_X-algebras.
items.locator: Lemma 2.11 with its proof, pp. 7–8, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (EGA I 9.5.8, 9.4.7; EGA IV₄ 18.12.13; EGA IV₂ 5.10.5; Stacks 0BK3, 0AW6; Kollár, Methods Appl. Anal. 24 (2017), Thm. 2)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): the final 'Moreover' clause was split off as item 65, to which E3 attaches. The locator now names the sources of the proof; its inputs are items 67 (Kollár's criterion), 69 (Zariski's main theorem), 70 ((S_2) of j_*), 71 (extension of coherent submodules), 63 (Ratliff) and 75 (schematic image).

items.name: Remark 2.12: weakening the hypothesis of Lemma 2.11
items.statement: Remark 2.12. The (S_2)-excellence of X in Lemma 2.11 may be weakened to the combination of §2.10's second condition with n = 2 and strict formal catenarity — every integral closed subscheme X' ⊂ X is strictly formally equidimensional, that is, Ô_{X',x} is equidimensional with no embedded associated primes for every x. Indeed, the first gives the openness of U_{(S_2)}(𝓜) and the second makes Ô_{closure of {u}, x} (S_1) and equidimensional.
items.locator: Remark 2.12 with its footnote, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (EGA IV₂ 7.2.1, 7.2.6)

items.name: Theorem 2.13: (S_2)-ification over an (S_2)-quasi-excellent base
items.statement: Theorem 2.13. For an open immersion j : U ↪ X of Noetherian, (S_2)-quasi-excellent schemes, an (S_2), finite U-scheme Ũ, and finitely many (S_2), coherent O_{Ũ}-modules 𝓜_i with |Supp(𝓜_i)| = |Ũ|, there are an (S_2), finite X-scheme X̃ and (S_2), coherent O_{X̃}-submodules 𝓜'_i ⊂ (j|_{X̃})_*(𝓜_i) with X̃|_U ≅ Ũ and 𝓜'_i|_{Ũ} = 𝓜_i, and in addition |Supp(𝓜'_i)| = |X̃| and O_{X̃} ↪ j_*(O_{Ũ}), so that O_{X̃} is (S_1) as an O_X-module.
items.locator: Theorem 2.13, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455

items.name: Corollary 2.14: every (S_2)-quasi-excellent scheme has an (S_2)-ification
items.statement: Corollary 2.14. Every Noetherian, (S_2)-quasi-excellent scheme X has an (S_2)-ification: a finite birational map X̃ → X that is an isomorphism over U_{(S_2)}(X), with X̃ being (S_2), locally equidimensional, (S_2)-excellent, and having U_{(S_2)}(X) as a dense open.
items.locator: Corollary 2.14, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455

items.name: The absence of a canonical (S_2)-ification
items.statement: For the reduction of the Macaulayfication problem to the CM-excellent case the principal complication is that there is no canonical (S_2)-ification morphism playing the role of the normalisation: Brodmann 3.9–3.11 confirms such absence. Even for (S_1) schemes, pushing the structure sheaf forward from the open (S_2) locus does not work, because the pushforward may fail to be coherent — for instance for a two-dimensional Noetherian local ring with an irreducible component of dimension 1. This is why Corollary 2.14 produces a noncanonical (S_2)-ification.
items.locator: §2, the paragraph before §2.8, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (Brodmann, 3.9–3.11)

items.name: Definition 3.1(ii): CM-secant sequences
items.statement: Definition 3.1(ii). For a finite module M over a Noetherian local ring (R,𝔪), a sequence r_1,…,r_s ∈ 𝔪 is CM-secant for M if it is secant for M (item 83), the module M/(r_1,…,r_s)M is Cohen–Macaulay, and for every 1 ≤ i ≤ s one has r_i ∈ ∏_{j < dim(Supp(M/(r_1,…,r_{i−1})M))} Ann_R(H^j_𝔪(R, M/(r_1,…,r_{i−1})M)), so that informally r_i vanishes to high enough order on the non-Cohen–Macaulay locus of M/(r_1,…,r_{i−1})M.
items.locator: Definition 3.1, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (Bourbaki, Algèbre commutative VIII, §3, no. 2, Def. 1)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): the definition was split: secant sequences (Definition 3.1(i)) are item 83, which belongs with systems of parameters in R03.3. dim(Supp(·)) is Mathlib's Module.supportDim (RingTheory/KrullDimension/Module.lean:32); CM-secant is in neither library.

items.name: Remark 3.2: secant sequences are parts of systems of parameters
items.statement: Remark 3.2. A sequence is secant for M if and only if it is part of a system of parameters for M: since dim(Supp(M/(r_1,…,r_{i−1})M)) − 1 ≤ dim(Supp(M/(r_1,…,r_i)M)), the sequence r_1,…,r_s is secant if and only if dim(Supp(M/(r_1,…,r_s)M)) = dim(Supp(M)) − s. Hence any permutation of a secant sequence is secant, as is r_1,…,r_{i−1},r_ir_j for 1 ≤ i ≤ j ≤ s, and any M-regular sequence is secant if M ≠ 0.
items.locator: Remark 3.2, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): moved from route 2 to the new R03.3 source route (route 4): it is the parameter-system theory that R03.3 is given by the accepted PAPER-ANDRE-18-B/secant-sequence and PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23/sop and /parameter-height. Mathlib has the displayed inequality and its equality cases: Module.supportDim_le_supportDim_quotSMulTop_succ, Module.supportDim_quotSMulTop_succ_eq_of_notMem_minimalPrimes_of_mem_maximalIdeal and Module.supportDim_add_length_eq_supportDim_of_isRegular (RingTheory/KrullDimension/Regular.lean:141, 151, 182).

items.name: Remark 3.3: Schenzel's bound on the failure of a secant sequence to be regular
items.statement: Remark 3.3. By a result of Schenzel, for a finite module M over a Noetherian local ring (R,𝔪) and any secant for M sequence r_1,…,r_s ∈ 𝔪 with s ≥ 1, the r_s-torsion of M/(r_1,…,r_{s−1})M is killed by ∏_{j < dim(Supp(M))} Ann_R(H^j_𝔪(R,M)). If M is Cohen–Macaulay this reconfirms that any such sequence is M-regular.
items.locator: Remark 3.3, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (Schenzel, Dualisierende Komplexe in der lokalen Algebra und Buchsbaum-Ringe, 2.4.2)

items.name: Remark 3.4: CM-secant systems of parameters are p-standard
items.statement: Remark 3.4. If r_1,…,r_s is a system of parameters for M then M/(r_1,…,r_s)M is 0-dimensional, hence Cohen–Macaulay; so in that case r_1,…,r_s is CM-secant for M if and only if r_s,…,r_1 is a p-standard system of parameters for M in the sense of Nguyen Tu Cuong, equivalently a p-standard system of parameters of type s − 1 in the sense of Kawasaki 2.6. Conversely any CM-secant sequence extends to a CM-secant system of parameters, because M/(r_1,…,r_s)M is Cohen–Macaulay.
items.locator: Remark 3.4, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (Nguyen Tu Cuong 2.4; Kawasaki, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 352 (2000), 2.6)

items.name: Local cohomology as a colimit of Ext
items.statement: For an ideal 𝔞 ⊂ R and an R-module M, H^i_𝔞(R,M) := colim_n Ext^i_R(R/𝔞^n, M). It may be computed over any family of ideals cofinal with the powers of 𝔞, in particular over all ideals whose radical contains 𝔞, and for Noetherian R it depends only on the radical of 𝔞.
items.locator: Used throughout §3, in particular in the proofs of Proposition 3.11 and Theorem 3.14, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (Stacks 0BJC, 0A6R, 0955, 0BJB)
items.note: Mathlib defines local cohomology as the colimit of Ext over the ideal-powers diagram, proves independence of the ideal up to radical and the comparison with the cofinal diagram of ideals with the same radical. It does not have the Čech complex computation, the composition spectral sequence or the H^1 identification, which are the parts actually used; those are recorded as additions in the Part II brief. Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): the item was split and its library claim narrowed. Mathlib (Algebra/Homology/LocalCohomology.lean:175, 180, 229, 263; the last two need [IsNoetherian R R]) has exactly this statement, and its 'Future work' list names the derived-functor description, the Čech complex and the long exact sequences as not done. Those, and the rest of the calculus the paper uses, are item 76 (missing, R03.3). The citation of idealPowersToSelfLERadical (:201), which is only the comparison functor, was replaced by the isomorphism isoSelfLERadical (:229).

items.name: §3.5: dualizing complexes over a Noetherian ring
items.statement: §3.5. For a Noetherian ring R, a complex ω^•_R is dualizing if its cohomology modules are finitely generated, its image in D(R) is isomorphic to a finite complex of injectives (so ω^•_R ∈ D^b_coh(R)) and R ≅ RHom_R(ω^•_R,ω^•_R) in D(R); then RHom_R(−,ω^•_R) is an involutive antiequivalence of D^b_coh(R). A dualizing complex is unique up to tensoring with an object that is Zariski-locally a shift of R; its formation commutes with localisation and with quotients, RHom_R(R',ω^•_R) being dualizing for R ↠ R'. For local R with residue field k, RHom_R(k,ω^•_R) is k in a single degree n, and ω^•_R is normalized if n = 0. By Kawasaki's theorem, which settled Sharp's conjecture, a Noetherian ring has a dualizing complex if and only if it is a quotient of a finite-dimensional Gorenstein ring; only the 'if' implication is used.
items.locator: §3.5 (Dualizing complexes), Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (Stacks 0A7B, 0A7C, 0A7F, 0A7G, 0A7I, 0DW7; Kawasaki, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 354 (2002), 1.4; Sharp 4.4)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): moved from route 2 to the new source route for Six-functor formalisms and analytic stacks AS.1 (route 5). The accepted routes 5 of PAPER-HACON-WITASZEK-23 ('Add its Noetherian singular dualizing-complex, finite-trace and local-duality adapters here') and PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23 (normalized dualizing complex) already send the Noetherian dualizing complex there, as missing source refinements; AS.1's own text does not plan it. Route 2's claim that the only dualizing complexes in the atlas are the perverse-sheaf ones was wrong: besides AS.1, Algebraic moduli A0-extension (via PAPER-PILLONI-20 route 10) supplies f^! for embeddable morphisms, and Tau Ceti StableReduction Layer 2 has the relative dualizing sheaf of Cohen–Macaulay curves, a different object. The existence, localisation and Cohen–Macaulay facts of §3.5 are items 80 and 81.

items.name: Lemma 3.6: the annihilator identity and the Cohen–Macaulay locus
items.statement: Lemma 3.6. Let (R,𝔪) be a Noetherian local ring with a normalized dualizing complex ω^•_R. (a) For every finite R-module M and every j ∈ Z, Ann_R(H^j_𝔪(R,M)) = Ann_R(H^{−j}(RHom_R(M,ω^•_R))). (b) For every finite M with equidimensional support, the ideal ∏_{j < dim(Supp(M))} Ann_R(H^j_𝔪(R,M)) = ∏_{j < dim(Supp(M))} Ann_R(H^{−j}(RHom_R(M,ω^•_R))) cuts out a closed subscheme of Spec(R) whose complement is the Cohen–Macaulay locus of M.
items.locator: Lemma 3.6 with its proof, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (Hartshorne, Residues and Duality V 6.2, or Schenzel 1.3.4, for local duality; Stacks 0A7Z, 0A7U)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): the locator now names the three inputs of the proof, which are items 79, 80 and 78.

items.name: Remark 3.7: the non-equidimensional case
items.statement: Remark 3.7. If the support of M in Lemma 3.6(b) is arbitrary then, by Schenzel 2.4.6, the product ideal cuts out a closed subscheme that set-theoretically equals {𝔭 ∈ Supp(M) : depth_{R_𝔭}(M_𝔭) + dim(R/𝔭) < dim(Supp(M))} and in particular contains every irreducible component of Supp(M) of non-maximal dimension.
items.locator: Remark 3.7, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (Schenzel 2.4.6)

items.name: Definition 3.8: d-sequences
items.statement: Definition 3.8. For a module M over a commutative ring R, a sequence r_1,…,r_s ∈ R is a d-sequence for M if for every i ≥ 1 scaling by r_i is injective on the submodule (r_1,…,r_s)M/(r_1,…,r_{i−1})M ⊂ M/(r_1,…,r_{i−1})M. This is a weak version of the definition of a regular sequence, originating with Huneke.
items.locator: Definition 3.8 with the sentence preceding it, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (Huneke, The theory of d-sequences and powers of ideals, Adv. Math. 46 (1982))

items.name: Remark 3.9: the equivalent torsion formulation of a d-sequence
items.statement: Remark 3.9. Definition 3.8 implies that the r_{i'}-torsion and the r_ir_{i'}-torsion submodules of M/(r_1,…,r_{i−1})M agree for every 1 ≤ i ≤ i' ≤ s, i.e. ((r_1,…,r_{i−1})M :_M r_ir_{i'}) = ((r_1,…,r_{i−1})M :_M r_{i'}) [the paper prints 'the r_i-torsion'; sourceIssues E5]. This is Huneke's formulation, often taken as the definition, and the two notions agree by Herrmann–Ikeda–Orbanz 38.6 b) and its proof.
items.locator: Remark 3.9, p. 12, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (Herrmann–Ikeda–Orbanz 38.6 b))
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): the statement had copied a misprint of the paper (E5).

items.name: Remark 3.10: the Goto–Yamagishi equalities for a d-sequence
items.statement: Remark 3.10. With 𝔯 := (r_1,…,r_s), a d-sequence satisfies ((r_1,…,r_{i−1})M :_M r_i) ∩ 𝔯^nM = (r_1,…,r_{i−1})M ∩ 𝔯^nM = (r_1,…,r_{i−1})𝔯^{n−1}M for every n ≥ 1 and 1 ≤ i ≤ s. The proof is by increasing induction on n and decreasing induction on i from the trivial cases i = s+1 and n = 1. The equality is due to Goto and Yamagishi and is also proved in Kawasaki 2.2.
items.locator: Remark 3.10 with display (3.10.1), Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455

items.name: Proposition 3.11: Kawasaki's properties of CM-secant sequences
items.statement: Proposition 3.11 (Kawasaki). For a finite module M over a Noetherian local ring (R,𝔪), any initial subsequence r_1,…,r_s of a CM-secant for M sequence r_1,…,r_s,…,r_s̃ satisfies, with I_j := ∏_{i=1}^{j}(r_1,…,r_i): (i) for any secant for M/(r_1,…,r_s)M sequence r'_1,…,r'_{s'} ∈ 𝔪 and M' := M/(r'_1,…,r'_{s'})M, the reversed sequence r_s,…,r_1 is a d-sequence for M'; (ii) for such a sequence and M', and for m,n > 0, the r_s^m-torsion and the (r_1,…,r_s)-torsion of M'/I_{s−1}^nM' coincide, so this torsion does not depend on m (the claim is vacuous when s ≤ 1); (iii) for such a sequence with M' := M/(r'_1,…,r'_{s'−1})M, if r'_{s'} is (M'/(r_1,…,r_s)M')-regular [the paper prints r_{s'}; sourceIssues E6] then it is M'-regular and (M'/I_s^nM')-regular for n > 0.
items.locator: Proposition 3.11 with the paragraph after it, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (Kawasaki, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 352 (2000), 2.9, 2.10, 3.1, 3.2, 3.3)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): clause (iii) had copied a misprint (E6). The paper does not reprove the proposition: (i) is a special case of Kaw00 2.10 via 2.9 and Remark 3.3, and (ii) and (iii) are special cases of Kaw00 3.2 and 3.3, which rest on Kaw00 3.1. The paper lists four misprints in Kaw00 that a formaliser reading it needs: in the last line of the proof of 2.8, 'n_{s+1},…,x_d' should be 'n_{s+1},…,n_d'; in the line before (3.1.5), and again before the last display of Step 3 of the proof of 3.1, 'y_u ∈ 𝔞(M/𝔮_kM)' should be 'y_u ∈ 𝔞(M/𝔮_kM) or y_u ∈ 𝔞(M)' (Kaw02 3.6 makes the same correction); in (3.1.6), 'y_1,…,y_{u−1}' should be 'y_1,…,y_u'; and in the last line of 3.3, 'k ≤ i ≤ j' should be 'k ≤ i ≤ j ≤ d'.

items.name: Remark 3.12: robustness of the conditions of Proposition 3.11
items.statement: Remark 3.12. The conditions (i)–(iii) of Proposition 3.11 are such that if a sequence r_1,…,r_s ∈ 𝔪 satisfies them, then it continues to do so after M is replaced by M/(r'_1,…,r'_{s'})M for any secant for M/(r_1,…,r_s)M sequence r'_1,…,r'_{s'} ∈ 𝔪.
items.locator: Remark 3.12, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455

items.name: §3.13: blowing up modules and strict transforms
items.statement: §3.13. For a scheme X, a quasi-coherent 𝓜 and a quasi-coherent ideal 𝓘, Bl_𝓘(𝓜) is the quasi-coherent O_{Bl_𝓘(X)}-module associated to the graded (⊕_{n≥0}𝓘^n)-module ⊕_{n≥0}𝓘^n𝓜; over an affine Spec(R) with I, M and i ∈ I, Γ(R_{(i)},Bl_𝓘(𝓜)) is the R_{(i)}-submodule M_{(i)} ⊂ M[1/i] generated by the image of M, so i is M_{(i)}-regular and Bl_𝓘(𝓜) has no nonzero sections supported on the exceptional divisor. The natural surjection 𝓜|_{Bl_𝓘(X)} ↠ Bl_𝓘(𝓜) is an isomorphism away from the vanishing locus of 𝓘 and its kernel consists of the local sections supported on the exceptional divisor, so Bl_𝓘(𝓜) is the strict transform of 𝓜 in the sense of Raynaud–Gruson I.5.1.1(ii). For a second ideal 𝓘' there are canonical identifications Bl_{𝓘𝓘'}(X) ≅ Bl_{𝓘·O}(Bl_{𝓘'}(X)) ≅ Bl_{𝓘'·O}(Bl_𝓘(X)) and the corresponding ones for Bl(𝓜).
items.locator: §3.13 (Blowing up modules), Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (Raynaud–Gruson I.5.1.1(ii); Stacks 080A)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): narrowed in scope, not in statement. Blowups of schemes, strict transforms, exceptional divisors and Stacks 080A for schemes are planned in Tau Ceti StableReduction Layer 4 (as in the accepted PAPER-BOXER-PILLONI-26/blow-up-exceptional-divisor-cartier), and the Raynaud–Gruson strict transform of a module in Adic coefficients and comparison with schemes L5 (PAPER-BOXER-PILLONI-26/flattening-by-blow-up). Route 2 imports both and adds Bl_𝓘(𝓜) = (⊕𝓘^n𝓜)~ for an arbitrary quasi-coherent 𝓜, its identification with that strict transform, and the module form of 080A.

items.name: Theorem 3.14: Kawasaki's Cohen–Macaulay blowing up
items.statement: Theorem 3.14 (Kawasaki). For a finite module M over a Noetherian local ring (R,𝔪) and a CM-secant for M sequence r_1,…,r_s̃ ∈ 𝔪, the product ideal I := ∏_{i=1}^{s̃}(r_1,…,r_i) is such that Bl_I(M) is a Cohen–Macaulay module on Bl_I(R). This is the paper's only source of Cohen–Macaulayness.
items.locator: Theorem 3.14, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (following Kawasaki, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 352 (2000), 4.1)

items.name: The proof of Theorem 3.14 and its two claims
items.statement: The proof works under the weaker hypothesis that every initial subsequence r_1,…,r_s (s ≤ s̃) satisfies conditions (i)–(iii) of Proposition 3.11 and that M̄ := M/(r_1,…,r_s̃)M is Cohen–Macaulay. The support of Bl_I(M) is the blowing up of Supp(M) at the restriction of I (Stacks 080E), of dimension ≤ dim(Supp(M)) (Herrmann–Ikeda–Orbanz 12.14), so it suffices to have depth ≥ dim(Supp(M)) at the closed points of the support. For an M̄-regular r' ∈ 𝔪, Proposition 3.11(iii) and the snake lemma make r' regular on ⊕I^nM with quotient ⊕I^n(M/r'M), and Remark 3.12 keeps the hypotheses, so one may pass to M/r'M; iterating, M̄ becomes 0-dimensional. Then, with I_s := ∏_{i=1}^{s}(r_1,…,r_i) [misprinted in the paper; sourceIssues E7], one shows by induction on s that depth(Bl_{I_s}(M)) ≥ s at the closed points of its support; the case s = 1 holds because r_1 is regular on Bl_{I_1}(M) ≅ M/M⟨r_1^∞⟩. For s ≥ 2, let R'' be the local ring of Bl_{I_s}(R) ≅ Bl_{(r_1,…,r_s)}(Bl_{I_{s−1}}(R)) at a closed point of the support, R' the local ring of Bl_{I_{s−1}}(R) at its image, and M'', M' the stalks; by induction depth_{R'}(M') ≥ s − 1. There is 1 ≤ i ≤ s − 1 with r_i generating (r_1,…,r_{s−1})R', R'- and M'-regular, and then (r_1,…,r_s)R' = (r_a,r_b)R' with {a,b} = {i,s}. Via the affine charts (Stacks 0804), R'' ≅ (R'[T]/(r_bT − r_a))_{(𝔪', f(T))}/(r_b-torsion) for a monic f, and Grothendieck's depth criterion (SGA 2 III 3.3(iv)) reduces depth_{R''}(M'') ≥ s to H^j_{𝔪''}(R'',M'') = 0 for j < s, which the spectral sequence, the Čech complex and the exact sequence of multiplication by r_bT − r_a reduce to two claims: Claim 3.14.5, that both r_i and r_s kill H^1_{(r_i,r_s)}(R',M'); and Claim 3.14.6, that H^j_{𝔪'}(R',H^{j'}_{(r_i,r_s)}(R',M')) = 0 for j < s − 2 and any j'. The claims are proved from conditions (i)–(ii), the regularity statements of §3.13, the inductive hypothesis for M and for the M/r_s^mM (Remark 3.12), the Čech complex and the composition spectral sequence.
items.locator: The proof of Theorem 3.14, including Claims 3.14.5 and 3.14.6, pp. 14–17, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (Herrmann–Ikeda–Orbanz 12.14; EGA I 9.5.5; EGA II 2.5.4, 2.5.6; SGA 2 III 3.3(iv); Stacks 0804, 080E, 0955, 0A6R, 0ALZ, 0BJB, 0BJC; EGA IV₁ 0.16.5.10(i))
