items.name: Blowing up a Cohen–Macaulay ring at a maximal ideal need not be Cohen–Macaulay
items.statement: Even if R is Cohen–Macaulay, the blowing up of R at a maximal ideal need not be Cohen–Macaulay, despite such centres being normally flat, equimultiple and normally Cohen–Macaulay; this is why Kawasaki's class of ideals in Theorem 3.14 is striking and why it is the backbone of the paper.
items.locator: §3, opening paragraph, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (Herrmann–Ikeda–Orbanz 14.11)

items.name: §4.1: biequidimensional schemes
items.statement: §4.1. A scheme X is biequidimensional if it is Noetherian, of finite dimension, and the saturated chains of specialisations of its points all have the same length, necessarily dim(X). Every biequidimensional X is locally equidimensional, and by EGA IV₂ 5.2.1 every connected, locally equidimensional X of finite type over a field is biequidimensional. If X is biequidimensional then so is every nowhere dense closed subscheme whose ideal sheaf is locally principal; conversely, if such an X' inside a Noetherian, catenary, locally equidimensional X contains all the closed points of X and is biequidimensional, then so is X, because all closed points of X then have height dim(X') + 1.
items.locator: §4.1 (Biequidimensionality) with its footnote, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (EGA IV₁ 0.14.3.3, corrected as in Illusie–Laszlo–Orgogozo XIV §2.4 footnote (i); EGA IV₂ 5.2.1; Heinrich, Some remarks on biequidimensionality of topological spaces and Noetherian schemes, J. Commut. Algebra 9 (2017), §3)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): the locator cited 'Heitmann §3'; the paper's [Hei17] is Katharina Heinrich's article in J. Commut. Algebra.

items.name: §4.2: dualizing complexes on schemes and their normalisation
items.statement: §4.2. For a Noetherian scheme X an object ω^•_X ∈ D^b_coh(O_X) is a dualizing complex if its restriction to every affine open is the image of a dualizing complex in the sense of §3.5. If X has one then so does every finite type, separated X-scheme, by Stacks 0AA3 and the Nagata compactification. If a Noetherian X with a dualizing complex is biequidimensional then, by Stacks 0AWF, there is a unique locally constant n such that for any x ∈ X of coheight δ(x) the complex (ω^•_X|_{O_{X,x}})[−δ(x)+n(x)] is a normalized dualizing complex for O_{X,x}; ω^•_X is called normalized when n = 0, which a unique locally constant shift arranges.
items.locator: §4.2 (Dualizing complexes on schemes), Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (Stacks 0A87, 0AA3, 0AWF, 0AX1)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): moved from route 1 to the AS.1 source route (route 5), for the reason given under item 39; the accepted PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23/dualizing and PAPER-HACON-WITASZEK-23/dualizing ask AS.1 for the same normalisation. Route 1 imports it.

items.name: Lemma 4.3: the Gabber–Liu–Lorenzini avoidance lemma
items.statement: Lemma 4.3 (Gabber–Liu–Lorenzini 5.1). For a Noetherian ring R, a projective R-scheme X, a closed subscheme Y ⊂ X that contains no positive-dimensional irreducible component of any R-fibre of X, points x_1,…,x_n ∈ X \ Y and a very R-ample line bundle 𝓛 on X, there are N > 0 and f ∈ Γ(X,𝓛^{⊗N}) such that the closed subscheme of X cut out by the coherent ideal im((𝓛^{⊗N})^{−1} →^f O_X) ⊂ O_X contains Y but contains none of the x_i.
items.locator: Lemma 4.3, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (Gabber–Liu–Lorenzini, Hypersurfaces in projective schemes and a moving lemma, Duke Math. J. 164 (2015), 5.1)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): the locator cited the wrong Gabber–Liu–Lorenzini paper ('The index of an algebraic variety'). The lemma is the Noetherian projective case of PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-22/avoidance (any ring, quasi-projective finitely presented X), which PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-22 route 7 proposes for SchemeAndStackFoundationsPartIIArithmeticPresentation (rejected pending revision, with the direction found justified) and whose id the accepted PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23 route 13 reuses; it moved from route 1 to a route reusing that id (route 6).

items.name: Proposition 4.4: Macaulayfication in the local case
items.statement: Proposition 4.4. For a complete Noetherian local ring (R,𝔪), a locally equidimensional, projective R-scheme X such that X_{R/𝔪} ⊂ X is a divisor and X \ X_{R/𝔪} is Cohen–Macaulay, and finitely many coherent O_X-modules 𝓜 with 𝓜|_{X \ X_{R/𝔪}} Cohen–Macaulay and |Supp(𝓜)| = |X|, there is a closed subscheme Z ⊂ X_{R/𝔪^n} for some n > 0 such that Bl_Z(X) is Cohen–Macaulay and so are all the coherent modules Bl_Z(𝓜).
items.locator: Proposition 4.4, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455

items.name: The construction in the proof of Proposition 4.4
items.statement: One reduces to X and X_{R/𝔪} connected, notes that X_{R/𝔪} and hence X are biequidimensional by Lemma 2.3(a) and §4.1, and takes a normalized dualizing complex ω^•_X. The coherent ideals 𝓘_𝓜 := ∏_{j<dim(X)} Ann_{O_X}(H^{−j}(RHom_{O_X}(𝓜,ω^•_X))) have, by biequidimensionality and Lemma 3.6(a), the stalks ∏_{j<dim(O_{X,x})} Ann(H^j_{𝔪(x)}(O_{X,x},𝓜_x)), so by Lemma 3.6(b) they cut out the complement of CM(𝓜); hence 𝓙_1 := (𝓘_{X_{R/𝔪}})^{N_0} ⊂ 𝓘_𝓜 for some N_0 > 0. One then builds a decreasing chain X ⊃ X_1 ⊃ ⋯ ⊃ X_d of biequidimensional closed subschemes of strictly decreasing dimension, X_1 := Spec(O_X/𝓙_1). Given X_m, stop with d := m if every 𝓜|_{X_m} is Cohen–Macaulay. Otherwise let ω^•_{X_m} := RHom_{O_X}(O_{X_m}, ω^•_X), which is normalized (Stacks 0AX1), and 𝓘_{𝓜,m} := ∏_{j<dim(X_m)} Ann_{O_{X_m}}(H^{−j}(RHom(𝓜|_{X_m}, ω^•_{X_m}))); it cuts out Y_{𝓜,m} := X_m \ CM(𝓜|_{X_m}), which contains no generic point of X_m. For a fixed very R-ample 𝓛, Lemma 4.3 gives N_m and f_m such that the locally principal 𝓙_{m+1} := im((𝓛^{⊗N_m})^{−1} →^{f_m} O_X) cuts out a closed subscheme containing each Y_{𝓜,m} and no generic point of X_m, and X_{m+1} := X_m ∩ V(𝓙_{m+1}) is biequidimensional of smaller dimension. With j_{m,x} a generator of (𝓙_m)_x, j_{d+1,x} := 1 and m_x the least m with j_{m+1,x} a unit, one needs j_{m+1,x} ∈ ∏_{j<dim O_{X_m,x}} Ann_{O_{X,x}}(H^j_{𝔪(x)}(O_{X,x}, (𝓜|_{X_m})_x)), the product taken in O_{X,x}; the paper's (4.4.1) asserts this for the preimage of 𝓘_{𝓜,m}, which can be larger, and the repair is to apply Lemma 4.3 to the closed subscheme of X cut out by the product of the O_X-annihilators, or to change j_{m+1,x} modulo (j_{1,x},…,j_{m,x}) [sourceIssues E9]. Then j_{1,x},…,j_{m_x,x} is CM-secant for every 𝓜_x, so Theorem 3.14 applies to the coherent ideal 𝓙 := ∏_{i=1}^{d}(𝓙_1,…,𝓙_i), whose stalks are the corresponding products; one takes Z := Spec(O_X/𝓙) and n := N_0·d.
items.locator: The proof of Proposition 4.4, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (EGA III₁ 5.5.1 for the connectedness of the special fibre; Stacks 0BJB, 0955, 0AX1)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): the middle of the statement was made precise (ω^•_{X_m}, 𝓘_{𝓜,m}, j_{m,x} and m_x were undefined, and 'contains the non-CM locus' is set-theoretic where Definition 3.1(ii) needs an ideal membership); the step needs the repair of E9. Its inputs are items 81, 82 and 53.

items.name: Lemma 5.1: composing two blowing ups is a blowing up
items.statement: Lemma 5.1. For a Noetherian scheme S, a closed subscheme Z ⊂ S with blowing up Bl_Z(S) →^b S, and a closed subscheme Z' ⊂ Bl_Z(S), there is a closed subscheme Z'' ⊂ S with |Z''| = |Z| ∪ b(|Z'|) and S-identifications Bl_{Z''}(S) ≅ Bl_{Z'}(Bl_Z(S)) and, for any quasi-coherent O_S-module 𝓜, Bl_{Z''}(𝓜) ≅ Bl_{Z'}(Bl_Z(𝓜)). The scheme statement is Stacks 080B; the module statement follows by interpreting both sides as strict transforms.
items.locator: Lemma 5.1, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (Stacks 080B; Raynaud–Gruson)

items.name: Proposition 5.2: Macaulayfication by one blowing up in the CM-excellent equidimensional case
items.statement: Proposition 5.2. For every CM-excellent, locally equidimensional, Noetherian scheme X and finitely many coherent O_X-modules 𝓜 with |Supp(𝓜)| = |X|, there is a closed subscheme Z ⊂ X disjoint from the dense open CM(X) ∩ ⋂_𝓜 CM(𝓜) such that Bl_Z(X) is Cohen–Macaulay and so are all the Bl_Z(𝓜).
items.locator: Proposition 5.2, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455

items.name: The Noetherian induction in the proof of Proposition 5.2
items.statement: Starting from an open U ⊊ X containing CM(X) ∩ ⋂_𝓜 CM(𝓜) for which the claim holds with a closed Z ⊂ U, one extends Z to a closed Z̃ ⊂ X by EGA I 9.4.7 and enlarges U using Lemma 5.1. Localising at a generic point of X \ U — legitimate by EGA I 9.4.7 and a limit argument using the openness of the Cohen–Macaulay loci of CM-excellent schemes — one may assume X = Spec(R) local with U the punctured spectrum, sets Y := Bl_{Z̃}(X) with its modules 𝓜̃ := Bl_{Z̃}(𝓜), and, by Lemma 5.1 again, precomposes with Bl_{Y_{R/𝔪}}(Y) → Y so that Y_{R/𝔪} ⊂ Y is a divisor. Since X is formally equidimensional, Lemma 2.3(b) makes Y_{R̂} locally equidimensional, and Lemma 2.4 transports the Cohen–Macaulayness of Y_U and its modules to the completion; Proposition 4.4 applies to Y_{R̂} → Spec(R̂) and gives Z ⊂ (Y_{R̂})_{R̂/𝔪^n} = Y_{R/𝔪^n}, so Z is a closed subscheme of Y disjoint from Y_U; since blowing up commutes with the flat base change R → R̂ (Stacks 0805), Bl_Z(Y_{R̂}) ≅ Bl_Z(Y)_{R̂}, and Lemma 2.4 descends the Cohen–Macaulayness to Y.
items.locator: The proof of Proposition 5.2, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (EGA I 9.4.7; Stacks 0805)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): the step that makes Z descend to Y (it lies in Y_{R/𝔪^n}) was missing. The base change is flat, not smooth, which is why blowups are imported from Tau Ceti StableReduction Layer 4 and not from Algebraic moduli R09.7a.

items.name: Theorem 5.3: the precise form of the main theorem
items.statement: Theorem 5.3. For every CM-quasi-excellent, Noetherian scheme X with finitely many coherent O_X-modules 𝓜 with |Supp(𝓜)| = |X|, there are a composition X̃ := Bl_Z(X') → X' →^{π'} X and, for each 𝓜, a coherent O_{X'}-module 𝓜' with |Supp(𝓜')| = |X'| such that X̃ and all the Bl_Z(𝓜') are Cohen–Macaulay and (i) X' is CM-excellent and locally equidimensional; (ii) π' is finite, birational and an isomorphism over U := U_{(S_2)}(X) ∩ ⋂_𝓜 U_{(S_2)}(𝓜), which is dense in both X and X' and on which 𝓜' ≅ 𝓜; (iii) Z ⊂ X' is disjoint from the dense open U' := CM(X') ∩ ⋂_𝓜 CM(𝓜'); (iv) U' is also dense in Bl_Z(X'), so X̃ → X is birational. If X is itself CM-excellent and locally equidimensional one may take X' = X and 𝓜' = 𝓜. The proof combines Theorem 2.13, Lemma 2.5 with §2.2, and Proposition 5.2.
items.locator: Theorem 5.3 with its proof, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455

items.name: Remark 5.4: the Macaulayfication is projective
items.statement: Remark 5.4. The map X̃ → X of Theorem 5.3 is projective, by EGA II 5.5.5(ii) and 6.1.11.
items.locator: Remark 5.4, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455

items.name: Proposition 5.5: the converse, sharpness of the hypothesis
items.statement: Proposition 5.5. Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme. If for every integral, closed subscheme X' ⊂ X there are a Cohen–Macaulay scheme X̃' and a proper map X̃' → X' that is an isomorphism over a nonempty open subscheme of X' — that is, a Macaulayfication of X' — then X is CM-quasi-excellent. It is an analogue of Grothendieck's EGA IV₂ 7.9.5, and the proof reduces to showing that the generic formal fibre of a local integral X is Cohen–Macaulay, using the identification of the completed local rings of X̃_{R̂} and X̃ at corresponding closed points and the ascent and descent of Cohen–Macaulayness along completion.
items.locator: Proposition 5.5 with its proof, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (EGA IV₂ 7.9.5, 7.9.3.1, 6.3.5)

items.name: §1.14: blowing up, with the properties the paper uses
items.statement: For a scheme X and a quasi-coherent ideal 𝓘 cutting out Y ⊂ X, Bl_Y(X) = Bl_𝓘(X) is the relative Proj of the Rees algebra ⊕_{n≥0}𝓘^n. The paper uses freely that it has the universal property (Stacks 0806), commutes with flat base change in X (Stacks 0805), and is projective over X when 𝓘 is of finite type (EGA II 5.5.2).
items.locator: §1.14 (Notation and conventions), second paragraph (Stacks 0806, 0805; EGA II 5.5.2), Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21. Split from item 17. Tau Ceti StableReduction Layer 4 plans 'the Rees algebra and the blowup of a quasi-coherent finite-type ideal as a relative Proj', with 'the universal property, properness/projectivity, compatibility with flat base change, behaviour away from the centre, exceptional divisor, strict transform, and affine chart descriptions'; RS-25 (accepted) gives relative Proj of finitely generated graded quasi-coherent algebras to Layer 2. The accepted PAPER-BENOIST-19/172 is planned in Layer 4 in the same way. Mathlib has the Rees algebra of an ideal (RingTheory/ReesAlgebra.lean:39) and no blowup. The blowups of non-finite-type ideals used in §3.13 (item 47) lie beyond Layer 4 and are covered there.

items.name: Ratliff's theorem
items.statement: A locally Noetherian scheme X is formally equidimensional if and only if it is locally equidimensional and universally catenary. In the form used in the proof of Lemma 2.11 (Stacks 0AW6): if X is universally catenary and x lies on the closure of a point u, then Ô_{closure({u}),x} is equidimensional.
items.locator: §2.2, p. 5; the proof of Lemma 2.11, p. 8 (Herrmann–Ikeda–Orbanz 18.17; Stacks 0AW6; Ratliff), Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21. Split from item 20, where it was a sentence of a definition. It is used in Corollary 2.14, Lemma 2.5 and Theorem 5.3 as well as in Lemma 2.11. Not in either library or in any atlas layer; R03.3 plans equidimensionality lemmas for finite modules, not this equivalence.

items.name: Lemma 2.3(b): formal equidimensionality is stable under blowing up
items.statement: Lemma 2.3(b). For a formally equidimensional scheme X and a coherent ideal 𝓘 ⊂ O_X, the blowing up Bl_𝓘(X) is formally equidimensional.
items.locator: Lemma 2.3(b) with its proof (Herrmann–Ikeda–Orbanz 18.26), Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21. Split from item 21. Used in Corollary 1.10 and in the proof of Proposition 5.2.

items.name: Lemma 2.11, final clause: an (S_2) extension without a direct sum
items.statement: Lemma 2.11 (final clause). In the situation of Lemma 2.11, if 𝓜 is (S_2) and for each x in the closure of Supp(𝓜) minus Supp(𝓜) that has height ≥ 2 in that closure the punctured spectrum of the local ring of the closure at x has no isolated points, then 𝓜' may be chosen to be (S_2) itself. [The proof does not return to this clause; sourceIssues E3 records the missing two lines.]
items.locator: Lemma 2.11, last sentence of the statement, p. 7; used in the last sentence of the proof of Theorem 2.13, p. 9, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21. Split from item 29 so that E3 attaches to it. It is the clause Theorem 2.13 uses to get (S_2) extensions 𝓜'_i rather than direct sums; checking its hypothesis there is also left implicit (E3).

items.name: Catenary (S_2) local rings are equidimensional
items.statement: A Noetherian local ring that is (S_2) and catenary is equidimensional (EGA IV₂ 5.10.9).
items.locator: Implicit in the proof of Lemma 2.5, p. 6 (the author's commented-out gloss at TeX l. 998 says this), and in the proof of Theorem 2.13, p. 9 (see sourceIssues E3), Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21. An equidimensionality lemma for local rings with a catenarity hypothesis, which is the kind R03.3 is asked to supply ('Give equidimensionality, associated-prime and support lemmas'; 'State hypotheses on catenarity'). Not in either library.

items.name: Kollár's coherence criterion for j_*
items.statement: For an open immersion j : U ↪ X of Noetherian schemes and a coherent O_U-module 𝓜, Stacks 0BK3 (Kollár, Coherence of local and global hulls, Thm. 2) gives a necessary and sufficient condition for j_*𝓜 to be coherent, in terms of the associated primes of the completed local rings of the closures of the associated points of 𝓜. As used: with X local, x its closed point and U the punctured spectrum, j_*𝓜 is coherent as soon as, for every associated point u ∈ U of 𝓜, every associated prime of Ô_{closure({u}),x} has coheight ≥ 2.
items.locator: The proof of Lemma 2.11, p. 8 (Stacks 0BK3; Kollár, Methods Appl. Anal. 24 (2017), Thm. 2), Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21. The engine of Lemma 2.11 and hence of the (S_2)-ification. Mathlib has only the quasi-coherence of pushforwards (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent_pushforward); nothing in the atlas mentions Kollár's criterion or Stacks 0BK3. The paper cites SGA 2 VIII 2.3 as the earlier criterion; that is PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-19/sga2-depth-coherence, sourced into Scheme and stack foundations SF.4 by an accepted route, so this item joins it there (route 3). The design job must take the exact hypotheses from Stacks 0BK3.

items.name: Formal patching along the completion
items.statement: For X = Spec(R) with R Noetherian local and U its punctured spectrum, coherent data on U and on Spec(R̂) that agree on U_{R̂} glue (Ferrand–Raynaud 4.2). Together with the commutation of j_* with the flat base change R → R̂, this reduces Theorem 2.13 to complete X: coherence descends by SGA 1 VIII 1.10 and (S_2) by Lemma 2.4.
items.locator: The proof of Theorem 2.13, p. 9 (Ferrand–Raynaud 4.2; SGA 1 VIII 1.10), Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21. The descent of finiteness along a faithfully flat map is in Mathlib (RingTheory/Finiteness/Descent.lean:36); the patching itself is in neither library or any layer. The design job must take the exact hypotheses from FR70 §4.

items.name: Zariski's main theorem, in the finite form used
items.statement: For X Noetherian local of dimension 1 with punctured spectrum U and a commutative coherent O_U-algebra 𝓜, 𝓜 extends to a commutative O_X-algebra that is coherent as an O_X-module (EGA IV₄ 18.12.13).
items.locator: The proof of Lemma 2.11, the case dim X = 1 for algebras, p. 8 (EGA IV₄ 18.12.13), Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21. Mathlib has Grothendieck's form, an open immersion into the integral (not necessarily finite) relative normalisation (AlgebraicGeometry/ZariskisMainTheorem.lean:206, Stacks 03GW); the finite form used here still needs a finite-subalgebra step.

items.name: (S_2) of j_* on a punctured spectrum
items.statement: For X Noetherian local with punctured spectrum j : U ↪ X and an (S_2) coherent O_U-module 𝓜 with j_*𝓜 coherent, j_*𝓜 is (S_2) (EGA IV₂ 5.10.5): H⁰_x and H¹_x of j_*𝓜 vanish, so its depth at x is ≥ 2.
items.locator: The proof of Lemma 2.11, p. 8 (EGA IV₂ 5.10.5), Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21. Imported and uncited in the extraction.

items.name: Extension of coherent submodules and closed subschemes across an open
items.statement: For a Noetherian scheme X, an open U ⊂ X with inclusion j and a coherent O_U-module 𝓜, there is a coherent O_X-submodule 𝓜' ⊂ j_*𝓜 with 𝓜'|_U = 𝓜 (EGA I 9.4.7); in particular every closed subscheme Z ⊂ U is Z̃ ∩ U for some closed subscheme Z̃ ⊂ X.
items.locator: The proof of Lemma 2.11, the case dim X = 1, p. 8; the proof of Proposition 5.2, twice, p. 20 (EGA I 9.4.7), Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21. Both checkers of §§2 and 5 found it independently. Scheme and stack foundations SF.0 constructs quasi-coherent modules but does not state this extension; it joins SF.0 as a source (route 3).

items.name: (S_n) along flat morphisms
items.statement: For a flat morphism g : X' → X of locally Noetherian schemes and a coherent O_X-module 𝓜: if g^*𝓜 is (S_n) then 𝓜 is; if 𝓜 is (S_n) and the fibres of g are (S_n), then g^*𝓜 is (S_n) (EGA IV₂ 6.4.1(i), 6.4.2). The local statement is the depth formula depth(M ⊗_A B) = depth(M) + depth(B/𝔪_AB) for a flat local homomorphism A → B. The proof of Lemma 2.4 also uses that (S_n) is kept by the base change of a formal fibre to a larger field.
items.locator: The proof of Lemma 2.4, p. 6 (EGA IV₂ 6.4.1(i), 6.4.2), Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21. R03.3 is asked to 'prove depth and dimension formulas under the local maps actually used'; this paper uses flat local maps, so it is a source for that clause (route 4). The scheme form is Zariski-local.

items.name: Divisors (effective Cartier divisors)
items.statement: A divisor in a scheme X is a closed subscheme whose ideal sheaf is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor. The paper never defines it, but uses it in Remark 1.7, Corollaries 1.10 and 1.11 and §4 (where X_{R/𝔪} ⊂ X is a divisor), and uses that the preimage of a divisor under a birational map to a scheme without embedded associated points is a divisor.
items.locator: Used in Remark 1.7, Corollaries 1.10 and 1.11 and §4, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21. Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge Layer C plans relative effective Cartier divisors, and ModularCurves 0A reuses that definition ('Use the shared definition: an effective Cartier divisor…'); the accepted PAPER-BOXER-PILLONI-26 cites Layer C for effective Cartier divisors in the same way. Tau Ceti's CartierDivisor (AlgebraicGeometry/CartierDivisor/Basic.lean) is the group of Cartier divisors, not the effective subscheme notion.

items.name: Birational morphisms
items.statement: A morphism π : X̃ → X is birational if it is an isomorphism over a dense open U ⊂ X whose preimage is dense in X̃ (this is how the proofs of Corollary 2.14 and Theorem 5.3 check it).
items.locator: Used in Theorem 1.6, Remark 1.7, Corollary 2.14 and Theorem 5.3, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21. Mathlib has birational equivalence of schemes through partial isomorphisms (AlgebraicGeometry/Birational/Birational.lean:39, 181) but no birational morphism; the design job defines it on top of PartialIso.

items.name: Schematic image and its compatibilities
items.statement: For a quasi-compact morphism f : Y → X the schematic image is the smallest closed subscheme through which f factors (EGA I 9.5.8); its formation commutes with flat base change and with localisation, as used to form 𝒳_0 in Corollary 1.8, to replace X by the schematic image of Ũ in Theorem 2.13, and in Lemma 2.11.
items.locator: Used in Corollary 1.8, Lemma 2.11 and Theorem 2.13 (EGA I 9.5.8), Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21. The construction is Mathlib's Scheme.Hom.image (AlgebraicGeometry/IdealSheaf/Subscheme.lean:661). L2 says 'Missing approximation, schematic closure, compactification … lemmas are owned here' and plans 'closure and plus-free scheme-theoretic constructions'.

items.name: The local cohomology calculus of §3
items.statement: For an ideal 𝔞 of a Noetherian ring R: the H^i_𝔞 are the right derived functors of 𝔞^∞-torsion, with long exact sequences; for 𝔞 = (a_1,…,a_n) they are computed by the Čech complex (Stacks 0A6R), so H^j_𝔞 = 0 for j > n, H^{≥1}_{(r)} vanishes on r^∞-torsion modules and H^1_{(r)}(R,M) ≅ colim_m M/r^mM with transition maps given by r; the spectral sequence H^j_𝔞(R, H^{j'}_𝔟(R,M)) ⇒ H^{j+j'}_{𝔞+𝔟}(R,M) (Stacks 0BJC, with 0955); independence of the base, H^j_𝔞(R,M) ≅ H^j_{𝔞R'}(R',M) for R'-modules M (Stacks 0BJB); and compatibility with localisation (Stacks 0ALZ), flat base change and filtered colimits.
items.locator: The proofs of Proposition 3.11 and Theorem 3.14 ((3.14.2)–(3.14.16)), pp. 13–17; (4.4.1), p. 19 (Stacks 0A6R, 0BJC, 0955, 0BJB, 0ALZ), Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21. Split from item 38. Mathlib's LocalCohomology.lean lists the derived-functor and Čech descriptions and the long exact sequences as future work. R03.3 is the owner: the accepted route 5 of PAPER-ANDRE-18-B refines 'the existing R03.3 Matlis/local-cohomology supplier' and asks R03.3 for the Noetherian Čech comparison (top-local-cohomology-tensor), and the accepted PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23/supported-cohom asks it for the Čech/Koszul models. This item joins them (route 4).

items.name: Grothendieck's depth criterion
items.statement: For a finite module M over a Noetherian local ring (R,𝔪) and n ≥ 0, depth(M) ≥ n if and only if H^j_𝔪(R,M) = 0 for all j < n (SGA 2 III 3.3(iv)).
items.locator: The proof of Theorem 3.14, before Claims 3.14.5 and 3.14.6, p. 16; both directions are used (SGA 2 III 3.3(iv)), Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21. R03.3 plans depth; the accepted PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-SCHOLZE-24/063 already records the vanishing half as planned in R03.3. With Rees's theorem in Mathlib (RingTheory/Depth/Rees.lean:158) and item 38 it is a short step, which R03.3 should take once for both directions.

items.name: The injective hull of the residue field and Matlis duality
items.statement: For a Noetherian local ring (R,𝔪) there is an injective hull E of R/𝔪; Hom_R(−,E) is exact, and for a finite R-module M', Hom_R(M',E) = 0 if and only if M' = 0, and Ann_R(M') = Ann_R(Hom_R(M',E)).
items.locator: The proof of Lemma 3.6(a), p. 11, Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21. Tau Ceti has the notion of an injective envelope and its uniqueness (Algebra/Module/Injective/Envelope.lean:101, 172) but not its existence. The accepted PAPER-ANDRE-18-B/residue-injective-hull, PAPER-HACON-WITASZEK-23/matlis and PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23/matlis are sourced into R03.3 for the same facts; this item joins them.

items.name: Local duality
items.statement: For a Noetherian local ring (R,𝔪) with a normalized dualizing complex ω^•_R and E the injective hull of R/𝔪, RΓ_𝔪(R,M) ≅ RHom_R(RHom_R(M,ω^•_R), E) naturally in M ∈ D^b_coh(R); hence H^j_𝔪(R,M) ≅ Hom_R(H^{−j}(RHom_R(M,ω^•_R)), E).
items.locator: The proof of Lemma 3.6(a), p. 11 (Hartshorne, Residues and Duality V 6.2; Schenzel 1.3.4), Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21. Joins AS.1 with items 39 and 52, which are 'the local-duality adapters' the accepted route 5 of PAPER-HACON-WITASZEK-23 asks AS.1 for; PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23/local-duality-a is the proper-scheme form.

items.name: Normalized dualizing complexes: existence over complete local rings, localisation and the Cohen–Macaulay criterion
items.statement: Every quotient of a finite-dimensional Gorenstein ring, in particular every complete Noetherian local ring, has a dualizing complex (Stacks 0DW7). For a Noetherian local R with normalized ω^•_R and 𝔭 of coheight δ(𝔭), (ω^•_R)_𝔭[−δ(𝔭)] is a normalized dualizing complex for R_𝔭 (Stacks 0A7Z). A finite R-module M is Cohen–Macaulay if and only if H^{−j}(RHom_R(M,ω^•_R)) = 0 for all j < dim(Supp(M)) (Stacks 0A7U); R itself is Cohen–Macaulay if and only if ω^•_R is concentrated in a single degree (Stacks 0AWS).
items.locator: §3.5, p. 10; the proof of Lemma 3.6(b), p. 11; Proposition 4.4, p. 18 (Stacks 0DW7, 0A7Z, 0A7U, 0AWS), Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21. The facts of §3.5 and Lemma 3.6 that item 39 left out. They belong with the normalized dualizing complex in AS.1.

items.name: Noetherian rings with a dualizing complex are CM-excellent
items.statement: A Noetherian ring R that has a dualizing complex is CM-excellent in the sense of Definition 1.2 (Stacks 0AWY, 0DW9, 0A80); in particular it is universally catenary, which is the catenarity used in the proof of Lemma 3.6(b).
items.locator: §3.5, p. 10; the proof of Lemma 3.6(b), p. 11 (Stacks 0AWY, 0DW9, 0A80), Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21. Stated in terms of the paper's CM-excellence (item 3), so it lives in route 1 with that notion and imports the dualizing complex from AS.1.

items.name: Zariski's connectedness theorem
items.statement: For a complete Noetherian local ring (R,𝔪) and a proper R-scheme X, the (R/𝔪)-fibre of each connected component of X is connected (EGA III₁ 5.5.1).
items.locator: The proof of Proposition 4.4, reduction to X and X_{R/𝔪} connected, p. 18 (EGA III₁ 5.5.1), Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21. No layer plans Zariski's connectedness or Stein factorisation. The theorem on formal functions it rests on is planned in Adic spaces Part II F0 ('formal functions and formal GAGA in the proper finite-presentation setting'), which route 1 imports.

items.name: Definition 3.1(i): secant sequences
items.statement: For a finite module M over a Noetherian local ring (R,𝔪), a sequence r_1,…,r_s ∈ 𝔪 is secant for M, in Bourbaki's sense, if dim(Supp(M/(r_1,…,r_i)M)) < dim(Supp(M/(r_1,…,r_{i−1})M)) for every 1 ≤ i ≤ s (with dim(∅) = −∞, so only the empty sequence is secant when M = 0).
items.locator: Definition 3.1(i) (Bourbaki, Algèbre commutative VIII, §3, no. 2, Def. 1), Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21. Split from item 34. Secant sequences are the partial systems of parameters of Remark 3.2 (item 35); R03.3 is given systems of parameters by the accepted PAPER-ANDRE-18-B/secant-sequence and PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23/sop, so this item joins them.

prerequisites.citation: Takesi Kawasaki, "On Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes", Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 352 (2000), no. 6, 2517–2552
prerequisites.why: The source of Proposition 3.11 and Theorem 3.14, the only source of Cohen–Macaulayness in the paper: p-standard systems of parameters (2.6), the Goto–Yamagishi equalities (2.2) and the theorem (4.1) that the blowing up of the product ideal built from such a system is Cohen–Macaulay. §3 reproves these in the module and CM-secant generality the paper needs, but the mathematics is Kawasaki's and the decomposition must start from his paper.

prerequisites.citation: Takesi Kawasaki, "On arithmetic Macaulayfication of Noetherian rings", Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 354 (2002), no. 1, 123–149
prerequisites.why: Theorem 1.4 settles Sharp's conjecture: a Noetherian ring has a dualizing complex if and only if it is a quotient of a finite-dimensional Gorenstein ring. Only the easy implication is used, but the equivalence is what makes §3.5's discussion of when a dualizing complex exists usable.

prerequisites.citation: Peter Schenzel, "Dualisierende Komplexe in der lokalen Algebra und Buchsbaum-Ringe", Lecture Notes in Mathematics 907, Springer (1982)
prerequisites.why: 2.4.2 is Remark 3.3, the statement that the product of the annihilators of the local cohomology modules kills the relevant torsion of a secant sequence, and 2.4.6 is Remark 3.7, the set-theoretic description of the locus it cuts out in the non-equidimensional case. These are what make the CM-secant condition checkable.

prerequisites.citation: Craig Huneke, "The theory of d-sequences and powers of ideals", Adv. Math. 46 (1982), no. 3, 249–279
prerequisites.why: The origin of the notion of a d-sequence, Definition 3.8, which is the weakening of regularity through which Kawasaki's argument runs.

prerequisites.citation: Manfred Herrmann, Shin Ikeda and Ulrich Orbanz, "Equimultiplicity and blowing up", Springer (1988)
prerequisites.why: 12.14 bounds the dimension of a blowing up, 14.11 gives the example of a Cohen–Macaulay ring whose blowing up at a maximal ideal is not Cohen–Macaulay, 18.17 is Ratliff's characterisation of formal equidimensionality, 18.20 and 18.26 are Lemma 2.3(a) and (b), and 38.6 b) is the equivalence of the two definitions of a d-sequence. Five separate results of this book are used and none is reproved.

prerequisites.citation: Ofer Gabber, Qing Liu and Dino Lorenzini, "Hypersurfaces in projective schemes and a moving lemma", Duke Math. J. 164 (2015), no. 7, 1187–1270
prerequisites.why: Lemma 5.1 there is Lemma 4.3 here, the avoidance lemma producing a section of a power of a very ample bundle whose zero scheme contains a prescribed closed subscheme and avoids prescribed points. It is what makes the inductive construction of §4 possible and is quoted without proof.

prerequisites.citation: Daniel Ferrand and Michel Raynaud, "Fibres formelles d'un anneau local noethérien", Ann. Sci. École Norm. Sup. (4) 3 (1970), 295–311
prerequisites.why: 3.3 is the two-dimensional Noetherian local (S_1) domain whose completion is not (S_1), which shows that the formal-fibre hypothesis in Lemma 2.4 cannot be dropped even for n = 1; 3.5 is the example showing that the (S_n) locus need not be open for n > 1; and 4.2 is the formal patching used in the proof of Theorem 2.13.

prerequisites.citation: János Kollár, "Coherence of local and global hulls", Methods Appl. Anal. 24 (2017), no. 1, 63–70 (Theorem 2; Stacks Project, Tag 0BK3)
prerequisites.why: The necessary and sufficient criterion for the coherence of j_*(𝓜) along an open immersion, in terms of the coheights of the associated primes of the completed local rings of the closures of the associated points. It is the engine of Lemma 2.11 and hence of the whole (S_2)-ification.

prerequisites.citation: Michel Raynaud and Laurent Gruson, "Critères de platitude et de projectivité", Invent. Math. 13 (1971), 1–89
prerequisites.why: I.5.1.1(ii) defines the strict transform of a module, which §3.13 identifies with Bl_𝓘(𝓜); the identification is used in Theorem 3.14, in Proposition 4.4 and in the module half of Lemma 5.1.

prerequisites.citation: Pierre Deligne, "Le théorème de plongement de Nagata", Kyoto J. Math. 50 (2010), no. 4, 661–670
prerequisites.why: 1.6 is the Nagata compactification, used for the integral model of Corollary 1.8, the compactification of Corollary 1.11, and the propagation of dualizing complexes along finite type separated maps in §4.2.

prerequisites.citation: A. Grothendieck and J. Dieudonné, EGA IV, Publ. Math. IHÉS 20, 24, 28, 32 (1964–1967)
prerequisites.why: The definitional backbone: 0.14.1.2, 0.14.3.3 and 0.16.5.4 for dimension, biequidimensionality and Cohen–Macaulayness; 2.3.4, 5.1.3, 5.2.1, 5.6.3(ii), 5.7.5, 5.10.5, 5.10.9, 5.11.4, 6.3.5, 6.3.7, 6.3.8, 6.4.1(i), 6.4.2, 6.11.6, 6.11.7(i), 6.11.8, 6.11.9, 7.1.1, 7.2.1, 7.2.2, 7.2.6, 7.3.8, 7.4.4, 7.8.2, 7.8.5, 7.9.3.1, 7.9.5 and 7.9.6 are each used for a specific statement. A blueprint cannot treat these as folklore.

Tags 0804, 0805, 0806, 080A, 080B, 080E, 0955, 0A6R, 0A7B, 0A7C, 0A7F, 0A7G, 0A7I, 0A7U, 0A7Z, 0A80, 0A87, 0AA3, 0ALZ, 0AW6, 0AWF, 0AWS, 0AWY, 0AX1, 0BJB, 0BJC, 0BK3, 0DW7 and 0DW9 are used by number for the blowup, dualizing-complex and local-cohomology facts. They are the intended proof sources for most of §§3.5, 3.13 and 4.2.

prerequisites.citation: Gerd Faltings, "Über Macaulayfizierung", Math. Ann. 238 (1978), no. 2, 175–192; Markus Brodmann, several papers (1983, 1986); Shiro Goto (1982); Peter Schenzel (1983); Takesi Kawasaki (1998, 2008); Morten Oskar Honsen, A compact moduli space for Cohen–Macaulay curves in projective space, PhD thesis, MIT (2004); Francesco Mordasini, On Macaulayfication of sheaves, Manuscripta Math. 99 (1999), 443–464; Katharina Heinrich, The space of Cohen–Macaulay curves, arXiv:1403.6082 (2014)
prerequisites.why: The previous constructions of Macaulayfications catalogued in §1.12, none of which preserves the Cohen–Macaulay locus except when the non-Cohen–Macaulay locus is a finite set of points. Faltings Satz 2 and Satz 3 are the origin of the problem and of the inductive method; Brodmann 3.9–3.11 is the proof that no canonical (S_2)-ification exists.

prerequisites.citation: Michael Temkin, "Desingularization of quasi-excellent schemes in characteristic zero", Adv. Math. 219 (2008), 488–522; Heisuke Hironaka, Ann. of Math. 79 (1964); A. J. de Jong, Publ. Math. IHÉS 83 (1996)
prerequisites.why: The status of Conjecture 1.1 that the paper's introduction records: Temkin's Theorem 1.1 in characteristic zero, building on Hironaka, and de Jong's alterations as the substitute in positive and mixed characteristic.

prerequisites.citation: Nguyen Tu Cuong, "p-standard systems of parameters and p-standard ideals in local rings", Acta Math. Vietnam. 20 (1995), no. 1, 145–161; Tetsushi Ogoma, "Noncatenary pseudogeometric normal rings", Japan. J. Math. (N.S.) 6 (1980), 147–163
prerequisites.why: The definition of a p-standard system of parameters compared with CM-secant sequences in Remark 3.4 (Cuong 2.4), and the appendix of Ogoma's paper, one of the two Noetherian noncatenary normal local domains that show in Remark 2.6 that the formal-fibre hypothesis of Lemma 2.5 cannot be dropped.

prerequisites.citation: Raymond C. Heitmann, "A noncatenary, normal, local domain", Rocky Mountain J. Math. 12 (1982), no. 1, 145–148
prerequisites.why: The other example cited in Remark 2.6 of a Noetherian noncatenary normal local domain.

prerequisites.citation: Katharina Heinrich, "Some remarks on biequidimensionality of topological spaces and Noetherian schemes", J. Commut. Algebra 9 (2017), no. 1, 49–63
prerequisites.why: §3 is cited in the footnote to §4.1 for the properties of biequidimensional schemes that the construction of Proposition 4.4 uses.

routes.title: Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations, Part II: excellence variants and Macaulayfication
routes.brief:
Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (arXiv:1810.04493v2), proves that every CM-quasi-excellent Noetherian scheme has a Macaulayfication. Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations (SchemeAndStackFoundations) SF.4 says that resolution is a theorem only in a named proved setting; this Part II builds such a setting, unconditional in all characteristics. It starts after SchemeAndStackFoundations and after its sibling Commutative algebra for deformation theory and patching, Part II: CM-secant sequences, d-sequences and Kawasaki's Cohen–Macaulay blowing ups (KawasakiCohenMacaulayBlowingUps), whose Theorem 3.14 is the only source of Cohen–Macaulayness in the argument.

Final theorems, as the paper states them. Theorem 1.6: for every CM-quasi-excellent, Noetherian scheme X, there are a Cohen–Macaulay scheme X̃ and a birational, projective morphism π: X̃ → X that is an isomorphism over the Cohen–Macaulay locus CM(X) ⊂ X. Theorem 5.3: for every CM-quasi-excellent, Noetherian scheme X equipped with finitely many coherent O_X-modules 𝓜 with |Supp(𝓜)| = |X|, there are a composition X̃ := Bl_Z(X') → X' →^{π'} X and for each 𝓜 a coherent O_{X'}-module 𝓜' for which |Supp(𝓜')| = |X'| such that X̃ is Cohen–Macaulay, its coherent modules Bl_Z(𝓜') are also all Cohen–Macaulay, and (i) X' is CM-excellent and locally equidimensional; (ii) π' is finite, birational, and is an isomorphism over the open U := U_{(S_2)}(X) ∩ (⋂_𝓜 U_{(S_2)}(𝓜)) ⊂ X that is dense in both X and X' and for which 𝓜'|_U ≅ 𝓜|_U; (iii) Z ⊂ X' is a closed subscheme that is disjoint from the dense open U' := CM(X') ∩ (⋂_𝓜 CM(𝓜')); (iv) U' is also dense in Bl_Z(X'), so that, in particular, the map X̃ → X is birational; if X itself is CM-excellent and locally equidimensional, then one may choose X' = X and 𝓜' = 𝓜. Remark 5.4: X̃ → X is projective. Corollary 1.8: for every integral Dedekind scheme S with the function field K and every proper, Cohen–Macaulay K-scheme X, there is a proper, flat, Cohen–Macaulay S-scheme 𝒳 with 𝒳_K ≃ X; if X is projective over K, then one may choose 𝒳 to be projective over S. Corollary 1.10: for every Noetherian, Cohen–Macaulay scheme X and every closed subscheme Z ⊂ X, there are a Cohen–Macaulay scheme X̃ and a projective morphism X̃ → X such that the scheme-theoretic preimage of Z in X̃ is a divisor and X̃ → X is an isomorphism over the maximal open subscheme U ⊂ X on which Z is already a divisor. Corollary 1.11: for every CM-quasi-excellent Noetherian scheme S and every finite type, separated S-scheme X that is Cohen–Macaulay, there is an open S-immersion X ↪ X̄ into a proper S-scheme X̄ that is Cohen–Macaulay such that X̄ \ X is a (possibly nonreduced) divisor in X̄ (the paper prints 'in X'; sourceIssues E1). Proposition 5.5: let X be a locally Noetherian scheme; if for every integral, closed subscheme X' ⊂ X there are a Cohen–Macaulay scheme X̃' and a proper map X̃' → X' that is an isomorphism over a nonempty open subscheme of X', then X is CM-quasi-excellent.

Construct here: quasi-excellence and excellence of schemes and the openness of Reg(X); CM-quasi-excellence and CM-excellence with the examples (quasi-excellent schemes, Dedekind schemes, closed subschemes of quasi-Cohen–Macaulay schemes) and their stability under localisation and finite type; universal catenarity of schemes, local and formal equidimensionality and Ratliff's theorem; the stability of formal equidimensionality under locally principal divisors and blowing up; the descent of (S_n) from the completion when the formal fibres are (S_n), with the Ferrand–Raynaud counterexample for n = 1; the openness of the (S_n) and Cohen–Macaulay loci under EGA IV₂ 6.11.6 and 6.11.8, with the Ferrand–Raynaud example; the (S_1)-ification; (S_n)-quasi-excellence; Lemma 2.11 with its final clause (E3), Zariski's main theorem in the finite form used, and the (S_2) property of j_*; formal patching along the completion; the noncanonical (S_2)-ification of Theorem 2.13 and Corollary 2.14, with Brodmann's absence of a canonical one; birational morphisms; biequidimensionality; the CM-excellence of rings with a dualizing complex; Zariski's connectedness theorem; the local Macaulayfication Proposition 4.4, with the repair of (4.4.1) (E9); the composition of blowups (Lemma 5.1); and the Noetherian induction of Proposition 5.2.

Two things must not be blurred. Quasi-excellence and CM-quasi-excellence are different conditions, and the theorem is new even for Q-schemes because the second is weaker. A Macaulayfication that does not preserve CM(X) is a strictly weaker statement, known earlier in several cases (Faltings, Brodmann, Kawasaki; §1.12); every corollary needs the isomorphy over CM(X).

routes.title: Commutative algebra for deformation theory and patching, Part II: CM-secant sequences, d-sequences and Kawasaki's Cohen–Macaulay blowing ups
routes.brief:
Section 3 of Česnavičius, Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), 1419–1455 (arXiv:1810.04493v2), reproves in module generality Kawasaki's construction of Cohen–Macaulay blowing ups (Kawasaki, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 352 (2000)), the engine of the Macaulayfication theorem. It starts after Commutative algebra for deformation theory and patching (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra) R03.3.

Final theorem, as the paper states it. Theorem 3.14 (Kawasaki): for a finite module M over a Noetherian, local ring (R, 𝔪) and a CM-secant for M sequence r_1, …, r_s̃ ∈ 𝔪, the product ideal I := ∏_{i=1}^{s̃} (r_1, …, r_i) is such that Bl_I(M) is a Cohen–Macaulay module on Bl_I(R). Its proof (item 49) is to be followed under the weaker hypothesis that every initial subsequence satisfies (i)–(iii) of Proposition 3.11 and M/(r_1,…,r_s̃)M is Cohen–Macaulay, and it must use the corrected I_s := ∏_{i=1}^s (r_1,…,r_i) (sourceIssues E7) and r_bT − r_a in (3.14.10) (E8). Even for Cohen–Macaulay R the blowing up at a maximal ideal need not be Cohen–Macaulay (HIO 14.11); Kawasaki's class of ideals is what makes the theorem possible.

Import, never re-plan: from Commutative algebra for deformation theory and patching (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra) R03.3, depth, Cohen–Macaulay modules, associated primes and support, secant sequences and systems of parameters (items 83, 35), the local cohomology calculus (item 76), Grothendieck's depth criterion (item 77) and the injective hull of the residue field (item 78); from Six-functor formalisms and analytic stacks (AnalyticStacks) AS.1, dualizing complexes over a Noetherian ring, their normalisation and localisation, and local duality (items 39, 79, 80); from Stable reduction of curves and stable maps (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction) Layer 4, blowups of schemes, strict transforms and affine charts; from Adic coefficients and comparison with schemes (AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons) L5, the Raynaud–Gruson strict transform of a module. Mathlib supplies regular sequences, Module.supportDim with its behaviour under quotients by parameters, derived categories and local cohomology as a colimit of Ext.

Construct here: CM-secant sequences (Definition 3.1(ii)) and their identification with p-standard systems of parameters (Remark 3.4); Schenzel's theorem that the product of the annihilators of local cohomology kills the relevant torsion of a secant sequence (Remark 3.3); the annihilator identity Ann(H^j_𝔪(M)) = Ann(H^{−j}(RHom(M, ω^•))) and, for equidimensional support, the cutting out of the non-Cohen–Macaulay locus by the product of these annihilators (Lemma 3.6), with Schenzel's set-theoretic description in general (Remark 3.7); d-sequences after Huneke, with the torsion formulation in its corrected form (Remark 3.9, E5) and the Goto–Yamagishi equalities; Kawasaki's Proposition 3.11 with the corrected clause (iii) (E6) and the robustness Remark 3.12; blowing up a module, its identification with the Raynaud–Gruson strict transform and the two-ideal identities (§3.13); and Theorem 3.14 with the two local-cohomology claims of its proof.

Secant, CM-secant, d-sequence and regular sequence are four different conditions and the proofs turn on exactly which one is available; do not collapse them. The definition of CM-secant is not symmetric in the r_i, and the reversal r_s, …, r_1 in Proposition 3.11(i) is not a typographical convenience.
routes.reason: R03.3 plans regular sequences, depth, Cohen–Macaulay modules and equidimensionality, and P9 depth and support for perfect complexes, but the roadmap plans no local cohomology beyond what Mathlib already defines and no dualizing complexes; the only dualizing complexes in the atlas are the perverse-sheaf ones of EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves, which are a different object. Kawasaki's construction of Cohen–Macaulay blowing ups, and the secant, CM-secant and d-sequence calculus it rests on, are reusable local algebra with consumers beyond this paper, so they belong in the commutative-algebra roadmap rather than inside the geometric Part II that consumes them. Review: accepted as corrected, retitled and renamed. The parent is right: Commutative algebra for deformation theory and patching is the atlas's local-algebra owner, and nothing plans CM-secant sequences, d-sequences, strict transforms of modules or Kawasaki's theorem. The scope was not. Local cohomology beyond Mathlib belongs to R03.3 (the accepted routes of PAPER-ANDRE-18-B and PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23). Dualizing complexes of Noetherian rings belong to AS.1 (the accepted routes 5 of PAPER-HACON-WITASZEK-23 and PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23). Secant sequences and systems of parameters belong to R03.3. Blowups of schemes belong to StableReduction Layer 4. The claim that the only dualizing complexes in the atlas are the perverse-sheaf ones was false. The brief cited 'AlgebraicModuli R09.7a', which is not an id, gave no titles, and claimed consumers beyond this paper, of which the atlas has none. So items 35 and 39 left for routes 4 and 5, the route was renamed from LocalCohomologyAndDualizingComplexes to KawasakiCohenMacaulayBlowingUps, and the brief was rewritten. The derived-category formalism comes from Mathlib, not EnhancedDerivedSheaves.

SF.0 constructs schemes and quasi-coherent modules, and the extension of a coherent submodule (or closed subscheme) across an open immersion of Noetherian schemes, EGA I 9.4.7 (item 71), used in Lemma 2.11 and twice in Proposition 5.2, is a basic statement about them that nothing states. SF.4 already receives the SGA 2 VIII 2.3 depth criteria for the coherence of local cohomology from the accepted route 4 of PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-19; Kollár's necessary and sufficient criterion for the coherence of j_* (Stacks 0BK3, item 67), which the paper cites as the successor of SGA 2 VIII 2.3, belongs beside it. Review (REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21): accepted as rewritten. The route first took only the Nagata compactification (item 13), which is planned in Adic coefficients and comparison with schemes L2, as its reason had missed; the review made the item planned and gave the route these two missing items instead.

Added by the review REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21. R03.3 is the atlas's owner of local commutative algebra: it develops depth and Cohen–Macaulay modules, proves 'depth and dimension formulas under the local maps actually used', gives 'equidimensionality, associated-prime and support lemmas', and states catenarity and excellence as hypotheses. Accepted routes have already given it systems of parameters (PAPER-ANDRE-18-B/secant-sequence, PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23/sop), the Noetherian local cohomology comparison and its Čech models (PAPER-ANDRE-18-B route 5, PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23/supported-cohom) and the residue-field injective hull with Matlis duality (PAPER-ANDRE-18-B, PAPER-HACON-WITASZEK-23, PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23). This paper is a source for the same targets in the exact forms §§2–3 use: secant sequences and Remark 3.2 (items 83, 35), the local cohomology calculus (76), Grothendieck's depth criterion (77), the injective hull (78), the flat depth formula behind (S_n) along flat maps (72) and the equidimensionality of catenary (S_2) local rings (66).

Added by the review REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21. Six-functor formalisms and analytic stacks AS.1 owns the quasi-coherent formalism and Grothendieck–Serre duality, and the accepted routes 5 of PAPER-HACON-WITASZEK-23 ('Add its Noetherian singular dualizing-complex, finite-trace and local-duality adapters here') and PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23 (normalized dualizing complex) have made it the single owner of dualizing complexes of Noetherian rings and schemes; the rejected route 3 of PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24, which put them in R03.3, confirms the choice. This paper is a source for the ring-level definition and its localisation and quotient properties (item 39), the normalisation on biequidimensional schemes (52), local duality (79), and existence over complete local rings with the Cohen–Macaulay criteria (80). If the maintainer judges AS.1, which sits on the ∞-categorical AS.0, too heavy a home for the Noetherian ring case, these items and the accepted ones should move together to a single new owner.

No generic rational-section or Grothendieck–Serre torsor target belongs to this geometry supplier. Do not assert nonflat base change for weighted blowups.
